Our mission is to counter the growing division and polarization by encouraging thoughtful conversations that prioritize respect, humility, and empathy. We aim to create an inclusive environment where all perspectives are welcomed and heard, as long as they are presented with civility and care.

club_name: Bridging The Gap at UCI - BTG
description: Our primary goal is to bridge the gap between socioeconomically disadvantaged students and careers in healthcare and research through an empowering culture of mentorship and service.

Brown Bag Theater Company is an ensemble of artists & scholars who aim to produce equally engaging & captivating artistic work that reflects & empowers the Latinx communities. We create various opportunities for young Latinx individuals, and our allies, within the performing arts. At BBTC, we believe that the discipline of theatre is a cultural force capable of transforming our community and we bolster this belief whilst celebrating the richness & pride of Latinx culture.

The purpose of built @uci is to provide an inclusive environment where students can explore their interests and strengthen their skills in any area they're passionate about, from crafting and design to technical building and problem-solving, through community meetings, workshops, and collaborative projects.

The organization, Burmese Student Associate (BURSA) at UCI, is dedicated to the celebration of Burmese culture as well as to creating a welcoming and supportive space for Burmese students. The organization aims to share Burmese culture and spread awareness of current events of the country within the University as well as the greater Los Angeles area. BURSA will allow the opportunity for students to engage in social, cultural, and community-service-based activities.

club_name: Business Careers in Entertainment Club at UCI
description: The Business Careers in Entertainment Club (BCEC) at UC Irvine was established during the Winter quarter of 2018. BCEC is designed to help students explore and prepare for careers in the entertainment industry. We're open to students of all majors, providing them with the professional development opportunities and network necessary to competitively pursue a career in entertainment. Whether you are interested in business development, finance, marketing, accounting, engineering, creative roles, or almost any other role in entertainment, BCEC can help you learn about those roles and/or strive to get them.

club_name: Business Law Society at UCI Law
description: The Business Law Society (BLS) is dedicated to bridging the gap between law students and the corporate and business sectors of the legal profession. The organization focuses on expanding professional networking opportunities by fostering connections with law firms, in-house counsel, and bar associations. BLS also aims to collaborate with other graduate programs and student organizations to host interdisciplinary events that promote the exchange of ideas and the development of meaningful professional relationships. In addition, the organization is committed to cultivating leadership skills and practical business acumen among its members through speaker panels, workshops, and targeted training sessions.

By Any Means (B.A.M.) is an organization dedicated to enriching the lives of the homeless by any means possible. We will cater to individual homeless shelters' unique needs, including supplying volunteers for particular programs or internships, collecting donations in the form of food, drink, or items and delivering donations to the shelters, and more. By Any Means will provide opportunities for volunteers to raise awareness for the homeless community, participate in/plan club events, and work with other organizations dedicated to helping the homeless.

club_name: Cal Animage Epsilon (formerly Anime Club-Cal Animage Epsilon)
description: To enrich students of UC Irvine with the language, culture and animation of Japan. And to unite people with similar interests in Japanese Animation.

club_name: CALPIRG - California Public Interest Research Group at UCI
description: Students have the power to shape the future we will inherit. We work with professional staff at colleges and universities to make sure our peers have the skills, opportunities and training they need to create a better, more sustainable future for all of us. Our chapters provide the training, professional support and resources students need to tackle climate change, protect public health, revitalize our democracy, feed the hungry and more. Students have been at the forefront of social change throughout history, from civil rights, to voting rights to protecting the environment. For nearly 50 years we’ve helped students to get organized, mobilized and energized so they can continue to be on the cutting edge of positive change.
The CalTeach Advisory Board recruits and cultivates community across and within cohorts to foster the collective well-being of future equity-focused teachers.

Cambodian Awareness Organization is a group dedicated to bringing Cambodia into the forefront of public thought. We celebrate multiculturalism and diversity among members. With a focus on social networking, building leadership skills, and volunteer experience, CAO encourages involvement in the community as we seek to reach out to people both at home and abroad. In addition, we are building bridges between student Cambodian organizations throughout Southern California.

Camp Kesem provides a summer camp to kids whose parents have been affected by cancer through the support of student-run campaigns. Kesem is a nationwide community, driven by passionate college student leaders, that supports children through and beyond their parents cancer. Kesem is the largest national organization dedicated to supporting children impacted by a parent's cancer at no cost to families. Our innovative and fun-filled programs provide children with peers who understand their unique needs and create long-lasting impacts.

CampMed at UCI aspires to inspire students who face low socioeconomic barriers to pursue higher education by providing exposure to undergraduate mentors, UC Irvine faculty, as well as healthcare professionals. CampMed at UCI is a student-run high school outreach program that was founded by UCI medical and undergraduate students in 1997. There was an increasing need for a local program that would target socio-economically disadvantaged high school students interested in pursuing higher education, particularly in the health science fields. Currently in its 27th year of existence, CampMed at UCI has reached out to over 5,000 high school students from Los Angeles and Orange County schools. In addition, the CampMed program has expanded to other UC campuses such as UCLA (2013), UC Riverside (2016), and UC Santa Barbara (2023).

Cards at UCI is dedicated to fostering a fun, inclusive community where students can learn, play, and connect through card and board games. Our mission is to introduce new card games, teach essential concepts in probability and statistics through gameplay, and create a relaxed social space for card enthusiasts to unwind from academic life.

CareTech is committed to advancing healthcare through the development of innovative applications designed for early disease detection, utilizing cutting-edge technologies and artificial intelligence. Our mission is to leverage the collective expertise of UCI students to create impactful solutions that significantly enhance healthcare outcomes.

club_name: Cariño Student Outreach Clinic (formerly Outreach Clinic at UC Irvine)
description: Cariño Student Outreach Clinic is a non-denominational organization that is committed to delivering high-quality medical care to individuals who have limited access to health services and insurance. We moved our operation to The HUB OC Resource Center to better serve the Santa Ana, Orange and neighboring communities. We strive to provide comprehensive care to our patients by offering health care services, wellness education, social services, basic medications, referrals, and, if they are eligible, assistance in obtaining health care coverage. While we would like to serve everyone, our clinic is intended to catch those who fall between the cracks of the current healthcare system, the uninsured.

Catalyst Undergraduate Art Gallery is an undergraduate-run gallery in which motivated students of any major may display their artwork while also gaining curatorial experience. Catalyst strives to promote budding artists' careers and to create opportunities for students to share art and culture with the campus at large.

club_name: Central Asian Student Association at UC Irvine
description: The mission of the Central Asian Student Association (CASA) at UC Irvine is to create unity among students from Central Asian backgrounds by fostering our shared cultural heritage while building deep and lasting connections. CASA strives to represent the voices of Central Asian students officially within UCI and beyond.Our purpose is to celebrate and preserve the unique traditions, history, and values of Central Asia through diverse activities that connect members to one another and to the broader academic and cultural community.In addition to cultural enrichment, CASA aims to highlight and share the achievements of Central Asian students in fields such as science, technology, arts, and more. By showcasing these accomplishments, we inspire current and future generations while building value and collaboration among members. CASA also seeks to make its presence well-known and accessible to new students from Central Asia at UCI, serving as a welcoming and supportive resource for those joining our community.

The primary purpose of Chabad at UCI is to provide an inclusive space for students at the University of California, Irvine to explore their Judaic roots within the framework of traditional Judaism. Our objectives include but are not limited to; educational, ritual, and social activities, in addition to counseling and spiritual guidance to individual students.

club_name: Charitable Humanitarian Acts Society at UCI - CHASO
description: CHASO is built upon the foundations of community and philanthropy. By uniting healthcare, business, and art under a common cause, we strive to provide resources for those underserved and raise awareness to societal issues. This chapter at UCI will focus on upbringing and highlighting small businesses nearby, while also connecting networks of current and past Anteaters to fundraise for the greater good.

The Chemistry Club aims to provide support for undergraduates at the University of California, Irvine, interested in the chemical sciences; we will promote scholarship, instill a mindset of career professionalism, emphasize the value of outreach, and build a community of individuals who will bond and grow—personally, academically, and professionally—in the field of chemistry.

The mission of Chi Rho Omicron shall be to promote the understanding, enrichment, and appreciation of the Pilipino culture, history, and heritage through a brotherhood/family environment. To instill the desire for self-improvement, scholastic excellence, and the cultivation of civic responsibility.

Our mission is to cultivate an inclusive community of Latinx and underrepresented students committed to addressing health disparities through service, education, and advocacy for underserved populations by fostering a diverse network.

Our organization aims to bridge the gap between incoming Chinese Anteaters and Chinese Alumni, who are willing to help students who studied abroad for the first time. By organizing workshops, group activities, and bonding events, we will hone students' life skills in living in the United States and achieving their pursuits. If you want to join a warm and supportive family, the Chinese Alumni Association is your best choice!

We, the members of the Chinese Association at the University of California-Irvine, establish this constitution to govern such matters as are within the jurisdiction of this organization. The purpose of CAUCI shall be threefold: a ) To increase the awareness of Chinese culture among club members/ associates and the general community; b ) To promote social interactions and understanding among members; c ) To be of service to the campus as well as surrounding community.

club_name: Chinese Dance & Ballet Fusion at UCI
description: We are dedicated to blending the grace of Chinese dance with the elegance of ballet, uniting the artistic essence of East and West. Through movement, we transcend cultural boundaries, fostering a community where tradition meets innovation, and every dancer finds their unique expression.

The purpose of this organization is to create a diverse learning environment and network for Chinese and other international students, facilitate conversations and promote awareness of Chinese-related laws and regulations, and assist member students and alumni in their career development.

Our organization intends to foster the love for Chinese traditional music through performances, collaborations and outreach. We wish to provide an open, supportive environment where students of all backgrounds can grow their skills, share their knowledge, and contribute to the multicultural fabric of UCI. We wish to share the experience of Chinese traditional music and explore its nexus with modern/western music.

CSSA is an organization that helps Chinese students and scholars in the aspects of daily life, career development in the U.S. Ourselves, members of CSSA-UCI, are a group of Chinese students and scholars who are full of passion and enthusiasm for exploring the way to building deep communication channels between Chinese and other cultures and groups at UCI. We want to build well organized community in which people with different nationalities have mutual understanding in culture identity.

Chinese Union (CU UCI) is a registered student organization at UCI founded by international students. we have been dedicated to serving the Chinese student community and supporting international students. CU UCI focuses on charity work, volunteer opportunities, and fostering cultural exchange within the campus community. CU provides valuable resources and networking opportunities for students. All active members receive a Volunteer Certificate as proof of their participation in CU's activities, and Executive Board members are recognized with a special certificate for their leadership roles.

club_name: Chinese Union in Computer Science - CUCS at UCI
description: Chinese Union in Computer Science mainly serves the Chinese students as well as other international students in the school of ICS, helps them improve the academic understanding and performance, enriches their extracurricular life and seeks intern/job opportunities for students. We hope that everyone can get great experience and valuable memory with CUCS.

club_name: Christian Legal Society Student Chapter at UCI School of Law (formerly Christian Law Students Association)
description: Christian Fellowship for UCI Law students.

Christian Students has been a registered club since 1974 at the University of California in Irvine. We hope that the club would serve as a gathering point for all students who are interested in pursuing the truth in the Bible and having fellowship with other students. We also organize other club activities to strengthen the bonds between members and to contribute to the overall atmosphere of student well-being and rapport on campus. If you are looking for a club that combines school life with spiritual life, then we invite you to join us!

Our mission is to encourage people to be familiar with what film has to offer and how to do it ourselves as well. We wish to explore every facet of the film industry while stimulating creativity on campus. We seek to establish a presence on campus that encourages all students to get involved in film discussion, understanding, and their production. This is a place for all people to engage/learn about how to make films together.

Circle K International (CKI) is a collegiate community service organization spanning the globe. We pursue our three tenets: service, leadership, and fellowship as we serve others. Circle K provides its members the opportunity to engage in communities both local and distant, with various colleges collaborating on projects across borders (often state and sometimes national) on a frequent basis. Additionally, the organization provides members with leadership opportunities and networking. Circle K is part of the Kiwanis Family, which includes community service groups at multiple levels of education and more. There is K-Kids for elementary school, Builder\'s Clubs for middle school, Key Clubs/KIWINs in high school, Circle K in colleges, CAYP for young professionals, and Aktion for the physically and mentally disabled, all of which are supported by Kiwanis International. Locally, Circle K at UC Irvine frequents community service projects all over. On a weekly basis we participate in helping out at Tabitha's Blessings, Save Our Youth, South County Outreach, Girls Inc., and Hemopet. During weekends, projects vary even more. However, we regularly volunteer for habitat restoration projects, like Second Sundays, various marathons and runs, community-wide food drives, and even animal-related service events, on top of any other events that need help in the area. Our organization strives towards membership development and community outreach by organizing and hosting fundraising events for the following district-wide initiatives: Kiwanis Family House, Pediatric Trauma Program, and American Foundation for Suicide Prevention. We are the leading global community-service organization on college and university campuses that enriches the world one member, one child and one community at a time.

Circle of Fifths is a student-run a cappella group that creates a space for members to join together and sing. Prioritizing showmanship and brotherhood, Circle of Fifths is a group whose energy and closeness are reflected closely in their performances. Circle of Fifths performs at club events on campus and outside events to which they are invited, and provides a space for tenor & bass singers to create memorable music. In addition to performance, Circle of Fifths also competes in competitions.

club_name: Civil and Environmental Engineering Graduate Association
description: The association's mission is to promote unity among CEE graduate students through social events, and advance their academic and professional interests. The idea behind the CEEGA association is to facilitate the interaction between graduate students from different sub-disciplines in CEE department. In order to attain this goal, various social events (including Pizza parties, Trekking, Board games etc) and scientific/professional events (including Career Panels, Workshops, Field Visits, etc) will be organized during each academic quarter. CEEGA will also provide networking opportunities with industry professionals and hold events to develop better interaction between current students and CEE Alumni. In addition, CEEGA will support and encourage CEE graduate student activities and events proposed by CEE graduate students and that are pertinent to CEEGA's vision.

Clair de Lune (CDL) A Cappella is an all-treble voice a cappella group at the University of California, Irvine. CDL is composed of members from various ethnicities, social classes, and levels of musical proficiency who come together to share their love for music and performance both on and off campus. We prioritize inclusivity and are a fully functioning support system for one another and strive to motivate each member to flourish musically as we become more confident in finding our voice as individuals, as well as in the ensemble!

Our mission is to promote meditative and mindfulness practices through a deep connection with the environment. We aim to facilitate collective action to address climate issues by organizing community cleanups, local initiatives, and environmental advocacy throughout the year to increase community ecological sustainability. Further, we are committed to advancing environmental education beyond our organization by collaborating with local climate change coalitions and field experts to educate our surrounding community.

Climbing Club at UCI is dedicated to promoting rock climbing within the UCI community. We achieve this by competing in the Collegiate Climbing Series (CCS) at the local, regional and national level competitions. We offer practices, training sessions, professional coaching, climbing specific clinics, and information meetings so everyone has the opportunity to increase their rock climbing knowledge and skill level.

Help improve members' skills by allowing each individual to compete at a high level. Develop friendships through the shared love of the game. Ensure members grow as teammates and individuals in order to cultivate success on and off the field. Make sure to follow us @uciclubbaseball for important information (tryouts, games, socials), or email us clubbasebalatuci@gmail.com with any questions!
To encourage students to not only learn more about Italian Culture and Language in an open environment, but also to engage students in study abroad opportunities and travel.

club_name: Club Roundnet at UCI (formerly Spikeball at UCI)
description: Club Roundnet at UCI is dedicated to fostering a vibrant community centered around the enjoyment and promotion of the game of Roundnet known more often as Spikeball. This club sport provides a place for competitive players to grow and compete against other colleges. As a part of the Spikeball College Tour series there will be two sectionals along with various other tournaments we will train for. The club consists of open pick up, competitive practices, clinics, exhibition matches, and national tournaments.
This club is a fastpitch softball team who competes around Southern California and parts of Arizona. Members have ranges of experience, but some experience is preferred due to the competitive level.
CSA aims to empower students interested in cognitive science by building a closer-knit community, making the Cognitive Science Department and research happening on campus more accessible.

College Democrats at UCI is dedicated to informing the student body about important political issues affecting our university, city, state, and country. We strive to foster intelligent political discussion and critical thinking on campus, connect students to their local communities and elected officials, and advance Democratic principles and policies of social, economic, and environmental justice.

College Republicans at UCI are dedicated to promoting political activism and providing a forum for debate here at UCI about issues concerning students, California, and the nation at large. We seek to bring together like-minded individuals in order to foster a greater sense of community. Whether you are a Republican or not, feel free to drop by and talk to us!
We are an organization at UC Irvine that delivers high quality software for non-profit organizations while providing meaningful opportunities for students to develop tech with purpose.

Common Ground Dance Team is an organization at UCI that is dedicated to growing as dancers and people, inspiring others through our performances at UCI and non-UCI events. Our mission, "Valuing the importance of well-being, self-expression, and inclusion; we strive to empower one another as a means to cultivate appreciation for our individualities - and although we may create, move, and live in different ways, one thing is for sure: DANCING IS OUR COMMON GROUND."

Communication Club seeks to foster a cultural and language exchangebetween UCI students and International ESL students. Through weeklyprogramming and the partnering of students, we aim to provide an outlet tothese international ESL students to make their experience at UCI better and topractice their English with fluent speakers.

The Community Health Alliance (CHA) of UCI is dedicated to raising awareness about the health and food insecurity issues faced by the homeless and underprivileged communities in underserved areas of Southern California. Our organization provides structured community support through various community service initiatives.

club_name: Community of Diverse Empowerment in Computing
description: CODEC is dedicated to making technology accessible while fostering a supportive, confident, and inclusive community for students interested in this field. We strive to create an environment where every student, particularly those who are underrepresented, new to technology, or uncertain about their place in the industry, feels welcomed, valued, and empowered to grow.Our mission is to assist students in finding their community, discovering their paths in the tech field, and developing the confidence necessary to thrive both academically and professionally. We believe that a sense of belonging is essential for success and that diversity, curiosity, and collaboration strengthen not only individuals but the entire tech community.By providing a non-judgmental space where questions are encouraged and experiences are shared, we aim to alleviate feelings of isolation, intimidation, and inadequacy. The community and personal development fostered by CODEC will support students throughout their time at UCI and equip them for success beyond their academic journeys.

club_name: Community Table at UCI (formerly Episcopal Campus Ministry at UCI (Canterbury Irvine))
description: The community table at UCI organization consists of a community of fellowship and service. We are a recognized group at the University of California, Irvine and we serve students, faculty, and staff with an emphasis on addressing the food insecurities that may exist in the college community. We meet once a month to have a communal meal with the members of the organization during which we express any ups and downs that have happened in our lives with the goal of fostering a strong support system among members to enhance the college experience. We have several community events throughout the year which involve spiritual growth, giving back to the community, study sessions, self-improvement workshops, and more.

Our mission is to allocate a space for artists and non-art majors to have a space to create art, learn about art, and be published in unjuried publications and exhibitions. The goals of our organization is to publish periodical print and digital publications unjuried, host an accessible gallery show of submitted artworks unjuried, and to build a community of artists that can create together and receive feedback from each other.

The mission of this organization is to:1. educate UC Irvine students about consumer law issues as well as legal andlegislative advocacy;2. create networks between consumer law attorneys, advocacy organizations, andthe UC Irvine student body;3. foster community among student advocates whose interests intersect withconsumer protection; and4. promote consumer protection curriculum and clinics that provide trainingopportunities for students.

The purpose(s) of this organization shall be to provide access to information about health care and the different careers in health care. Furthermore, the club is not only for the career, but to allow students to engage in community service, health-related education, and clinical experience. The club will also serve as a platform for the COPE Health Scholars program, affiliated with the clinical educational program, to advocate for improvements.

To support fellowship on campus and to bring the experience of the Orthodox Christian Church through community life, prayer, service to others, and study of the Faith. Furthermore, Coptic Club @ UCI strives to nurture and strengthen love for Christ Jesus and His church in its fullness at this most critical juncture of life.

The purpose of CCS is to promote research in the cosmetic industry to further the interests and recognition of aspiring cosmetic chemists. Through events and workshops, CCS will help students interested in the cosmetic industry to get connected with industry professionals, gain insight on and opportunities in the field, and learn about the chemical ingredients and their interactions in personal care products. CCS will be career and professionally focused, but the organization will also emphasize the creativity, educational, and social aspects of the cosmetic industry.

At Create For Kids, we use the power of art to bring smiles to hospitalized children. We know that being in a hospital can be tough for kids and their families, which is why we provide a variety of creative activities to make their stay a little brighter. We believe that art is a vital component of the healing process, and we strive to create a nurturing environment that promotes creativity and smiles. Our volunteers are passionate about their work and are dedicated to making a lasting impact on children's lives.

The CMN’s mission is to foster a collaborative environment in which filmmakers, actors, writers, photographers, and all persons interested in the creative process can connect with one another through a streamlined and accessible network. The CMN will serve as a community through which the creative process can be shared. The CMN is completely led by and for UCI students and will focus on catering to their creative efforts, but all CMN resources will be available to anyone regardless of experience or university affiliation. Our initial goals for the organization involve its inception as a website for filmmakers, actors, and all other creatives to post job boards, advertise their skills, and promote upcoming projects or events. This site will also include a search function, which will allow collaborators to find and contact members who match their needs. Following this initial establishment, the CMN wishes to expand its scope and outreach through quarterly membership-recruitment activities and educational workshops, as well as social networking events for established members.

The purpose of the organization is to provide a supportive and creative environment where individuals can explore art as a tool for personal growth, emotional healing, and self-expression. The club's mission is to foster mental and emotional well-being through artistic activities, workshops, lectures, and clinical experiences that allow participants to engage in a therapeutic process. In the short term, the organization aims to offer regular sessions that introduce various art forms, providing participants with space and guidance to express their emotions in a safe and non-judgmental setting. Also, having professional therapists across multiple disciplines lecture during meetings, members will have a unique opportunity to learn what the profession is like. The long-term goal is to inevitably create a close-knit community where like-minded members at UCI can develop their creative skills, gain clinical experience, promote mental wellness, and raise awareness about the benefits of art therapy. The club's audience includes students, faculty, and community members who are interested in the intersection of art and mental health, regardless of their prior experience in art. The organization is dedicated to making a positive impact on the mental health landscape by offering a unique and accessible approach to therapy that combines creativity with emotional support.

club_name: Creative Writers Guild at UC Irvine
description: We are an organization that promotes and celebrates the processes of creative writing. We recognize the power of narrative in our culture, and our goal is to craft stories, poems, and films that matter.

The Cricket Club at UCI plays and hosts the prestigious OCCA (Orange County Cricket Association) which involves the best cricket playing clubs in Orange County. The tournament is held in the Fall Quarter and Winter Quarter every year and played in the Twenty-20 overs format. We also play competitive bilateral series games against our arch rivals UC San Diego on non-league weekends.

The purpose of our Criminology, Law and Society Club is to offer a space of similar majors and interests to students who would like to network with others of the same degree aspiration. We want to provide insight, guidance, and services to support students with their classes as well as a pathway for success. Our goal is to allow students to have an open space to collaborate, study, and hear from guest speakers about career opportunities and their experiences within the field. We decided to create this club as there is no environment for Criminology students to gather and support each other.

Cross Youth Initiative at UCI is a dynamic collegiate campus group dedicated to reaching and empowering the next generation through a unique blend of faith and sports. Partnering with faith-based youth organizations, we organize spontaneous sports meetups, competitive tournaments, and engaging sports camps for middle and high school students. Our mission is to inspire and mentor youth by combining athletic activities with the teachings of Christ. College students serve as coaches and role models, building meaningful relationships and providing positive guidance. Join us in fostering a community where sports and spirituality come together to create lasting impacts on young lives through the Cross Youth Initiative. Partnering with faith-based youth organizations, we organize spontaneous sports meetups, competitive tournaments, and engaging sports camps for middle and high school students. Our mission is to inspire and mentor youth by combining athletic activities with the teachings of Christ. College students serve as coaches and role models, building meaningful relationships and providing positive guidance. Join us in fostering a community where sports and spirituality come together to create lasting impacts on young lives through the Cross Youth Initiative at UCI.
To bring Gospel-loving students together to enjoy fellowship and grow in the Word.

club_name: Crossroads at UCI (formerly Liberty Campus Connect at UCI)
description: Knowing God and making Him known through Bible study, worship, and Christ-centered community.
We are Cru, a multiethnic community of students and staff passionate about Jesus. We exist to know God better, grow in our faith together, and show the love of Jesus to the world.

Cyber@UCI is the premier applied cybersecurity education resource at UCI that focuses on delivering cybersecurity education and awareness to the local community and student population. We accomplish this through organizing and hosting weekly meetings, independent student research, and competitions. We provide a space and community for students, staff, and faculty to experiment and learn about cybersecurity however it pertains to their personal and/or professional interests.
Cycling Club at UCI offers resources so as to assist those interested in pursuing mountain biking or road biking as a competitive club sport, recreation hobby, or healthy life style.

D¡tto is in reference to the transforming copy-cat Pokémon and composition by NJZ (a K-pop group), building a connection to our mission of allowing students to become whoever they want to be and providing a shared space where people can share passion, creativity, and cultural exchange. D¡tto aims to provide new experiences to students wanting to learn how to dance or admire Korean culture. Therefore, this club is built to encourage members to learn, move, and grow together.

Established in 2021, Data @ UCI aims to promote and grow the field of Data Science: providing resources to students who are interested in data or related fields to succeed in college and in their careers. We provide workshops that provide knowledge to supplement analytical skills needed in the industry and research. We are a student-run organization ultimately dedicated to the community of UCI and Orange County.
Delight's mission is to invite college women into Christ-centered community that fosters vulnerability and transforms stories.

The purpose of Delta Delta Delta shall be to establish a perpetual bond of friendship among its members, to develop a stronger and more womanly character, to broaden the moral and intellectual life, and to assist its members in every possible way. It shall also be the purpose of Delta Delta Delta to promote and develop mutually beneficial relationships between the Fraternity and the colleges and universities where the Fraternity has established chapters, to develop qualities of unselfish leadership among its members, and to encourage them to assume, with integrity and devotion to moral and democratic principles, the highest responsibilities of college women.

The mission of Delta Delta Sigma is to provide students with community service opportunities and guidance towards a career in dentistry. We aspire to help students build a strong professional foundation with real world, hands-on experiences such as clinical volunteering, mission trips, and health fairs. We urge our members to value the necessity of serving those in underserved communities while also reinforcing academic integrity on the road towards dental school. Members will have the opportunity to network with dental students, alumni, dental professionals, and fellow pre-dentals. Delta Delta Sigma welcomes all students interested in health care professions to attain exposure to the exciting world of dentistry.

Delta Epsilon Mu is a professional health-interest fraternity at UCI that provides a dynamic educational and social setting for all undergraduates striving toward goals in human and veterinary medicine, pharmacy, dentistry, optometry, nursing, and other health fields.

Delta Gamma offers to women of all ages a rich heritage; continuity based on sound and tested principals of personal integrity, personal responsibility, and intellectual honesty. The object of this Fraternity shall be to foster high ideals of friendship among college women, to promote their educational and cultural interests, to create in them a true sense of social responsibility and to develop in them the best qualities of character.

Delta Lambda Chi aspires to bond dignified individuals who are dedicated to the values of moral excellence and everlasting sisterhood. As we strive to elicit the highest quality in service, leadership, and academic aptitude, we also commit ourselves to experiences that enhance our character and enrich our minds. The memories we share mark an indelible journey through our college years that is symbolic of loyalty, perseverance, and personal achievement. Delta Lambda Chi, Alpha Chapter. We are founded on February 9, 2002, at the University of California, Irvine. Our motto is "reach for the stars but remain down to earth."

Delta Sigma Pi is a professional fraternity organized to foster the study of business in universities; to encourage scholarship, social activity and the association of students for their mutual advancement by research and practice; to promote closer affiliation between the commercial world and students of commerce, and to further a higher standard of commercial ethics and culture and the civic and commercial welfare of the community.

Delta Sigma Theta Sorority, Inc. was founded on January 13, 1913, on the campus of Howard University by twenty-two collegiate women that wanted to use their collective strengths to promote academic excellence and provide assistance to those in need. The Founders of Delta Sigma Theta envisioned an organization committed to sisterhood, scholarship, service, and addressing the social issues of the time. Since its founding, Delta Sigma Theta has become one of the preeminent service-based sororities, with more than 350,000 initiated members and over 1,050 chartered chapters worldwide. In March of 1913, Delta Sigma Theta performed their first of public service by participating in the Women's Suffrage March in Washington D.C. The Xi Omega Chapter was chartered on the UCI campus on May 31, 1980, by fifteen remarkable women. Since its inception, the chapter, consisting of women of higher character, integrity and great accomplishments, has been actively participating in service aimed at the advancement of the African American community. Historically, some of our service includes voter registration drive, educational workshops, cultural awareness workshops, and annual scholarship donations.

The purpose of this organization is to provide volunteer opportunities for pre-health students who wish to participate in volunteer opportunities, with a focus on dental. Our audience will include students, underserved children, older adults in nursing homes, and other underserved communities. Through volunteering, we will also teach our volunteers dental knowledge such as tray setup, dental instruments, dental etiquette, clinical photography, dental school preparation, and more.

Design at UCI is a community for designers of all skill levels and backgrounds. We provide the resources and space for students to innovate, create, and ultimately grow as designers. Through community, education, and collaboration, we strive to spark and foster creativity in our members and throughout the UCI community.
The mission of this organization is to create a supportive and stigma-reducing space for students, faculty, staff, and campus affiliates to learn about the complexities of managing diabetes

Guided by the belief that there is always a better version of oneself, Dialogue Society aims to enrich the lives of communities. Our purpose is to educate the community through meaningful dialogues on healthy, purposeful and mindful living—free from promoting political affiliations or religious beliefs—to discover what inspires us towards personal development. We move forward by the motto of "Dialogue. Discover. Develop."

The purpose of this organization is to provide students with events catered to enriching their knowledge of filmmaking and expose themselves to professionals working in the industry. We also strive to connect students with resources and each other in order to promote filmmaking at UCI.

The Disability and Neurodiversity Alliance Plus is a support and advocacy group of undergraduate students at UC Irvine. We are led by students with disabilities including people who identify as d/Deaf, autistic, and allies of people with disabilities, represented by the “Plus” in our name. We aim to make our club a safe space to destigmatize disability identity and create opportunities for self-advocacy and mutual aid. DNA+ will further raise awareness of accessibility while also creating a campus culture supportive of students with disabilities.

club_name: Diverse Abilities Inclusion & Support for Youth
description: Diverse Abilities Inclusion & Support for Youth aims at raising awareness about the importance of inclusivity as well as the obstacles that children with diverse disabilities face. In order to achieve this, DAISY works alongside children with various temporary and chronic disabilities, including cognitive and physical conditions, to help improve their quality of life, inspire them to reach their full potentials, and offer a strong network of peers and support.

We aim to inform and raise awareness among the broader community about global conflicts and ways individuals can support these efforts, whether through fundraising, education, or resource provision. Additionally, our commitment extends to assisting individuals irrespective of their gender, political beliefs, or religious affiliation.

Dragon Boat at UC Irvine is a team that competes at dragon boat festivals, racing against other college teams and non-college teams. Dragon boat is a sport consisting of twenty paddlers in a long canoe shaped boat, paddling simultaneously. We are heading into our 24th year of existence and have races in San Francisco; Tempe, AZ; Long Beach; San Diego; and even Vancouver. We are a team that strives to exceed expectations in our training and competition. Along with training, our team aims to build strong bonds and create a big family. With this sense of family and competition, we strive to represent UCI at the best of our ability at every race.

At Drainers at UCI, our mission is to foster a safe, inclusive, and vibrant community centered around a shared passion for underground music. We aim to bring together students who seek connection through niche genres and emerging artists, providing a space where they can discover new sounds, express themselves, and build meaningful relationships. In the short term, we strive to cultivate a supportive environment for fans to meet and engage with one another. In the long term, we aspire to grow a lasting network of friendships rooted in a love for underground music and authentic connection.

DreamCatchers at UCI develops students into compassionate leaders through fostering intergenerational connections between students and older adults, particularly those who are in hospice. These connections are created through acts of service, primarily by fulfilling end-of-life Dreams for hospice patients.

Young adults are more isolated and misinformed about the psychologies and substances that alter them now more than ever. The dichotomy of drug use lies in the fact that while we become more open to substance use, its consequences multiply in severity. Now, more than ever, discussing intervention methods that provide factual data and real-world improvements is critical.This student-led organization promotes safe driving, safe alcohol and substance use habits, and safety among young adults, specifically those within Orange County. The organization strives to promote these ideals through guidance, advocacy, awareness, and intervention against impaired driving.

ESSC is an academic and social club that focuses on providing guidance, professional development opportunities, and a place for students to meet others interested in environmental careers. All majors are welcome!

EASA’s mission is to foster a strong, inclusive community for East African students at UCI by celebrating our cultures, uplifting underrepresented voices, and creating a space where students feel seen, supported, and empowered. We aim to connect students through shared identity and experience, and promote cultural pride through events, dialogue, and mentorship.

Echolalia: Undergraduate Literary Journal's purpose is to create a safe and non-discriminatory environment for all students of University California, Irvine to express their literary voices in an accessible publication. Echolalia will be working to make a difference by providing a resourceful outlet and promoting interests in literature, and creative, as well as academic writing by means of disseminating a publication.

club_name: Ecology and Evolutionary Club at UCI
description: The purpose of EEB Club is to create a community for those involved in the EEB major or interested in EEB. We will highlight community and volunteer events, resources for students, connect with faculty and peers etc.
To provide a community filled with Egyptians or people interested in Egyptian culture. To create a space for Egyptians to meet one another and to create connections here at UCI.
Our mission is to make resources that prevent opioid overdoses readily available to the UCI community and beyond, and to raise public awareness of drug-related deaths and how they can be prevented.

It is the mission of the Engineering Student Council (ESC) at UC Irvine to be a liaison between undergraduate engineering students and the faculty, staff, and administration of The Henry Samueli School of Engineering. ESC serves as the umbrella organization for other Engineering Student Organizations to promote cooperation and build relationships among students. We create networking and research opportunities for students by coordinating events with other organizations, faculty members, and corporations across Southern California. As student leaders, we envision and advocate for the educational, social, and professional advancement of the engineering community.

club_name: Engineers for a Sustainable World at UCI - ESW
description: Engineers for a Sustainable World (ESW) at UCI is a chapter of a non-profit organization that is committed to building a greener world and welcomes students of all majors (engineering and non engineering) that believe in need to improve our environment. ESW focuses on designing sustainable engineering projects, professional development and educating members on sustainability. Our events include alumni panels, networking opportunities, tours to facilities, and our projects range from building solar charging stations, cultivating algae for bio-fuel, to designing piezoelectric objects. This organization would be a great way to get more students involved with hands-on projects and spread awareness about sustainability.

The purpose of EWB-UCI shall reflect and support the values and mission of Engineers Without Borders-USA: “to partner with disadvantaged communities to improve their quality of life through implementation of environmentally sound and economically sustainable engineering projects, while developing internationally responsible engineering students.”

The English Majors' Association (EMA) works to bring together students and faculty to build a sense of community within the English Department and a support system for current undergraduate students. Although the club is primarily aimed towards students in the English major/minor, we also welcome students from the Literary Journalism and Comparative Literature programs, as well as anyone who is interested in discussing literature! EMA holds regular weekly meetings as well as quarterly events such as Book Swaps, Poetry Events, Open Mic Nights, Research Presentations, and Game Nights.

The Entertainment and Sports Law Society is a student-run organization focused on incorporating business and legal studies involving music, film, fashion, video games, sports, and other industries of interest. Our organization hosts speaker presentations, social events, and provides networking opportunities in an effort to circulate industry information and contacts within the entertainment and sports law sector. The organization will also create a publication informing the UCI Law community about current issues and legal decisions affecting the industry at large.

club_name: Environmental Law Society at University of California Irvine School of Law
description: We are a group of student activists eager to learn about local, national, and global environmental challenges. Our hope is to explore the wide variety of opportunities for environmental lawyers and policymakers to enact change. ELS also aims to bring together community leaders interested in all types and scales of environmental issues. Our events will address issues surrounding environmental justice, the climate crisis, biodiversity, and habitat loss. We plan to host speakers, inform students of job opportunities, network with other student groups at UCI and around the country, help students connect with professionals in environmental law, conduct greening activities, and participate in advocacy campaigns.

Eta Kappa Nu is the student honor society of IEEE and is dedicated to encouraging and recognizing excellence in the IEEE-designated fields of interest. Members consist of students, alumni, and other professionals who have demonstrated exceptional academic and professional accomplishments. Student members are selected on the basis of scholastic standing, character, and leadership. Through a variety of service programs and leadership training, student members develop lifelong skills that earmark them for prominent positions in industry and academia. Members are much better prepared for the post-college world and are especially valuable and attractive to employers. They are recognized as extremely capable, both technically and professionally. After graduation, members continue their involvement through their university chapters, volunteering for IEEE-HKN committees and receiving information on IEEE-HKN activities. To further recognize excellence, IEEE-HKN conducts award programs to recognize professional leaders, exceptional educators, outstanding students, young engineering professionals, outstanding chapters, and effective faculty advisors. For more than 100 years, Eta Kappa Nu has embraced excellence. In the years ahead, IEEE-HKN will continue to reinvent itself to meet the needs of its members, the institutions they serve, and our overall society.

This organization exists to develop and promote interest in classical study among the students of colleges and universities; to promote closer relationships among students who are interested in classical study, including inter-campus relationships; to engage generally in an effort to stimulate interest in classical study, and in the languages, literature, history, and art of ancient Greece and Rome.

club_name: Euphonic Video Game Ensemble at UCI
description: To provide musicians, artists, and other video game/enthusiasts a safe space & creative outlet to express their love for their favorite media.
Educate members on the principles of autonomous vehicles while also designing algorithms and competing the F1Tenth car at robotics competitions.

club_name: FADA Film Arts Drama Alliance Network at UCI
description: FADA is an organization dedicated to networking student filmmakers and promoting collaborative filmmaking. We sponsor weekly ZOTFILM production meetings, where club members can enjoy producing short-films with other members of the UCI film community. All of this will culminate in our student-run film festival and celebration, ZOTFEST, at the end of the year.

club_name: Fashion and Sneakers at UCI -FS at UCI
description: FSUCI aims to make fashion more than just a hobby. FSUCI celebrates fashion as a powerful form of self-identity and is committed to building a place where students creatively express themselves in any way they wish. Members can share their experiences and tastes in fashion and feel uplifted by club members regardless of differing opinions in the fashion community through hands-on experiences and community-driven events that incorporate fashion as a medium. Additionally, we aim to introduce undergraduate students to career pathways within the fashion and apparel industry.

club_name: Fashion Collective at UCI (formerly Anteater Atelier Fashion Club)
description: Providing creatives across UCI a platform to work collectively towards building community and defining the future of fashion.

club_name: Federal Bar Association (FBA) Law School Student Chapter
description: We are committed to fostering the highest standards of professionalism and legal competence among law students at UCI. Our mission is to provide opportunities for professional development, networking, and service to the community. We aim to bridge the gap between students and the federal legal profession by facilitating meaningful interactions with practitioners, judges, and public servants in the federal system. We strive to enhance understanding of federal law and the federal legal system, promote the welfare and interests of law students, and contribute to the advancement of justice under the law.

Founded in 1982, the Federalist Society for Law and Public Policy Studies is a group of conservatives and libertarians dedicated to reforming the current legal order. We are committed to the principles that the state exists to preserve freedom, that the separation of governmental powers is central to our Constitution, and that it is emphatically the province and duty of the judiciary to say what the law is, not what it should be. The Society seeks to promote awareness of these principles and to further their application through its activities and welcomes all interested in exploring these principles.

Fencing Club at UCI competes at the collegiate level against other schools in Southern California. We encourage everyone interested in fencing to join us for practice. We welcome beginners and experienced fencers alike. Equipment and instruction are provided. Drop by and check us out!

FightingGamers@UCI (FG@UCI) is a student organization on the campus of the University of California, Irvine (UCI) for people who have an interest in fighting games. What began as a small club for UCI students, FG@UCI is now a community comprised of SoCal's most passionate fighting gamers. Our goal is to host gatherings where fighting gamers can meet, play, and grow with others. We accomplish this by providing a positive and enriching environment through our weekly sessions and special events, all held at UCI and open to the public. We strive to provide our members with resources necessary to enable their passion for fighting games. Weekly meetings take place on Tuesdays at the UCI Esports Arena from 6:30 PM to midnight. Feel free to stop by, and join our Discord for club updates! https://discord.gg/xHhSeaQ

The purpose of Figure Skating Club at UCI is to promote the sport of figure skating within the Irvine community and provide ways for its members to progress in and enjoy the sport as a team and as individuals. We are committed to community service and outreach and seek to build a community of skaters who train together, encourage and support each other, and celebrate each others' accomplishments.

Our mission is to build a humble community of God, united with the Catholic Church, to foster the spiritual growth of young adults through our Marian devotion and response to the Holy Spirit. Liwanag strives to become disciples of Jesus, servants to servants, and a light to all.

club_name: Filipinx Undergraduate Scientist-Engineers In an Organized Network (FUSION) (formerly Filipinos Unifying Scientist-Engineers In an Organized Network)
description: FUSION exists to provide a community that fosters the personal and professional growth of members through the facets of the science & engineering field and Filipino culture.

The goal of the Financial Literacy Association shall be to aid undergraduate University of California, Irvine students to make better and more informed decisions regarding the use and management of money.

club_name: First Generation Professionals Program at UCI Law
description: FGP seeks to foster an inclusive UCI Law community that supports first-generation, economically underrepresented and/or non-traditional law students as well as their support networks including partners, family, and communities. FGP is an organization that not only provides a shared space to reflect on these experiences, but also fosters academic success, self-care and personal support for our members' personal well-being and professional aptitude. FGP members further seeks to build on UCI Law's goal of building a diverse law school student body, and offer programming that creates a more diverse law pipeline. FGP is centered on principles that support these goals rather than a single identity.

The Fishing Club at UCI’s mission is to facilitate and foster the sport/hobby of fishing among the UCI student populace and the importance of fish and wildlife conservation. This club is also intended to be an outlet that readily provides fishing opportunities and community space for those familiar with and new to the sport and hobby.

This organization is an undergraduate-run branch of the Southern California Chapter of The Flying Samaritans, a registered 501(c)(3) non-profit organization. The UCI chapter is not an independent 501(c)(3) entity and operates under the oversight of The Flying Samaritans. We are committed to facilitating the service efforts of The Flying Samaritans, Inc., a registered non-profit corporation. Students, physicians, dentists, optometrists, pilots, and other healthcare practitioners travel monthly to medical clinics located throughout Mexico to provide free, quality healthcare to those who would otherwise lack access.Healthcare is provided to the people living in the rural areas outside of Tecate, Mexico in our student-run clinic, Clinica Jose Lemus Lopez Heroes del Desierto Mexico in El Testerazo. At our clinic, our members have the opportunity to assist in administrating, translating, and taking vital signs. Furthermore, students are able to witness the clinic flow and view different aspects of primary care from: intake, assessment, diagnosis, and discharge. Our members can experience healthcare and immerse themselves in another culture firsthand, both of which are incredibly educational and rewarding.

In September 2011 Food Recovery Network (FRN) was founded as a student group at the University of Maryland. Today, we're the largest student movement fighting against food waste and hunger and have recovered and donated more than 3.9 million pounds of food that otherwise would have gone to waste. That's more than 3.2 million meals that's gone to those in need. It is also more than 6.8 million pounds of carbon dioxide prevented from reaching the atmosphere.

Women and minorities are still sorely absent from directing, producing, stage management, and administrative positions in the theater and entertainment industry. Forte Theater Company pledges to prioritize, encourage, and value the involvement of women and minorities not only in the selection of performance material, but in decision-making and leadership positions. FTC will be a space for women and minorities to gain leadership and artistic experience that will equip them with life, work, and social skills to support their goals and success long after UCI graduation. Club structures like the Creative Committee, Communications and Value Officer, and quarterly Feedback Forums ensure diversity in leadership and decision making, constant upkeep of club values, and consistent opportunities for self-reflection and accountability. FTC will provide more performance opportunities for underclassmen and underrepresented students. FTC plans to have at least one freshman-only performance opportunity per year, helping UCI first-years gain performance experience that can otherwise be very difficult to find in UCI’s competitive theater program. This will ease the transition into collegiate theater for drama majors, and provide opportunities for freshman students of all majors to connect with peers, express themselves, and expand their comfort zones. FTC plans to perform student-written work, elevate underrepresented stories and progressive revivals, encourage participation of non-arts majors, and increase connectivity between dance, drama, and music students at UCI. FTC pledges to have at least one performance with content voted on through Activity Elections. This will allow the UC Irvine community both inside and outside the club to share what work they’d like to see and representation gaps we could help fill.FTC also seeks to create more approachable and accessible non-audition creative events like open mics and workshops. UC Irvine is a high-level and competitive institution, especially in drama spaces, and this can be intimidating, especially to minorities, transfer students, non-drama majors, and first-year students. Our commitment to inclusion, accessibility, and prioritizing collaborative art creation over competition will make FTC a unique and invaluable environment for countless UC Irvine students.

Our mission is to provide quality patient centered health care to the underserved community within Orange County, with an emphasis on educating future healthcare professionals and increasing awareness of the health care disparity through our continual research.

club_name: French and Francophone Club at UCI
description: The mission of the French and Francophone Club at UCI is to connect students who have an interest and or passion in the French language and francophone culture at UCI. The French and Francophone Club at UCI encourages students of all backgrounds to learn more about the francophone world.

Furries at UCI is a social club for UCI students within the furry fandom, a community that takes interest in anthropomorphic animal characters. We aim to create a safe environment for students to connect with others within the furry fandom, foster friendships, receive support from peers, and freely express their creativity and personality through unique animal characters. We host regular meetings for club members to socialize and play games, as well as provide resources for local furry events.

Gamma Phi Beta was founded November 11, 1874 at Syracuse University. Our mission is to promote the highest form of womanhood through education, social life and service to humanity. Our founders, Helen M. Dodge, Francis E. Haven, E. Adeline Curtis and Mary A. Bingham started this organization to foster a nurturing environment that provides women the opportunity to achieve their potential.

club_name: General Chemistry Peer Mentoring at UCI
description: Our mission is to provide free guidance to UCI undergraduates seeking reliable academic support from peers, primarily in general chemistry coursework. We also aim to encourage and mentor undergraduates who are interested in general chemistry.

club_name: Genetic Counseling Special Interest Group at UCI - GCSIG
description: The purpose of this organization is to provide students with the opportunity to learn more about the field of genetic counseling. Additionally, students will gain first-hand experience discussing genetic disorders, speaking and making connections with different kinds of genetic counselors, and learn about different graduate programs available for the field.

Our mission is to promote female weight lifting while empowering all gender-identities to feel strong and beautiful in a judgement-free community. Whether you're a dedicated gym goer or a curious beginner, Girl Gains is here to support you in every stage of your fitness journey.

Global Business Brigades is a secular, student-operated volunteer organization that partners with Global Brigades, an international nonprofit organization, to empower communities without proper access to economic resources in Ghana, Guatemala, Honduras, Nicaragua, Panama, and Greece. This empowerment involves partnering with such communities to provide sustainable financial opportunities and assistance after a holistic review of each community’s specific needs, with the ultimate goal of community ownership of a sustainable healthcare system. Global Business Brigades is the business-centric chapter within the organization, targeting the countries Honduras, Panama, and Greece.

Global Dental Brigades is an international movement of students and healthcare professionals working alongside local communities and staff to implement sustainable health systems. We work in remote, rural, and under resourced communities in Honduras, Panama, Guatemala, Belize, Ghana, and Greece, which would otherwise have limited to no access to health care.

club_name: Global Health Research Education And Translation Club
description: Global Health Research, Education, and Translation (GHREAT) is dedicated to promoting awareness of global health issues in the UCI community through the analysis of news, trends, and research literature. We place an emphasis on global health research and communication, completing one research project per academic year. By creating an open and engaging forum for the discussion of global health topics, members will increase their understanding of global health issues both at home and abroad through an interdisciplinary lens.

The Global Medical Brigades (GMB) nonprofit partners with communities in Guatemala, Honduras, Panama, Nicaragua, Greece, and Ghana to form and staff free clinics for populations without proper access to healthcare. During the spring or summer of each year, our club travels to one of these clinics and/or works with clinic staff during a virtual "telebrigade." Before these programs, our club at UCI works to raise funds for the clinics and programming and learns about international healthcare. Although the format for any given program depends on members' interests and finances, participants are guaranteed opportunities to shadow doctors, learn about international treatments and medications, and work directly with patients in a variety of specialties. Through funding the in-person or virtual programs, our club directly supports GMB international clinics and empowers communities to build sustainable healthcare systems.

Global Medical Missions Alliance is a Christian healthcare organization that strives to fulfill the Great Commission of Jesus Christ by equipping the next generation of future healthcare leaders and professionals. It provides a unique community and fellowship among peers and mentors committed to medical missions and healing ministries. There are many opportunities for training, networking, short-term local and abroad medical missions.

The purpose of Global Medical Training as an organization is to provide aid and healthcare to underserved communities around the world. Established in 2008 as the third chapter of GMT within the UC system, we are a humanitarian organization for students of premedical, pre-pharmacy, pre-dental, and all other pre-health professions focusing on serving vulnerable populations. We travel abroad to Latin American countries such as Panama, Nicaragua, Peru, and the Dominican Republic to hold free medical clinics for underserved communities. We prepare the students who partake in our medical mission trips by hosting mock clinics, workshops, and orientations prior to their departure. Locally, we foster a sense of community through various events such as workshops, socials, and volunteer events. These opportunities allow members to also engage with and support local populations. GMT UCI creates the opportunity to acquire unique, hands-on experiences unlike any other volunteer work.

The mission of GoodSoil at UCI is to provide a platform for Chinese-speaking students or English-speaking students who want to learn Chinese at UC Irvine to receive Christian faith based on Jesus's teachings in the Holy Bible.

club_name: Google Developer Group on Campus at UCI
description: Google Developer Group on Campus at UCI works to empower students of UC Irvine to connect, learn, and grow by fostering an inclusive developer community, bridging the gap between academic theory and industry practice, and creating opportunities for collaboration among students, faculty, industry professionals, and the broader Google developer ecosystem.

The purpose of this organization is to provide a place of community for students at UCI who are interested in, wish to become involved in, or learn about the goth subculture as well as other alternative subcultures.

club_name: Graduate Association of Biomedical Engineering Students-GABES
description: Graduate Association of Biomedical Engineering Students (GABES) at UC Irvine seeks to facilitate networking between students, industry, alumni, and the larger Orange County biomedical community. We aim to provide avenues that will allow graduate students to build experience in leadership and communications, skills essential for professional development.

The mission of Grad PHA is to cultivate a vibrant and inclusive community that enriches the graduate experience for public health students. We are dedicated to fostering a safe and engaging environment where diversity is celebrated, and every student feels valued and connected. Our commitment is to enhance the academic and social journey of our members through innovative activities and events that promote collaboration, well-being, and professional growth. By focusing on these pillars, Grad PHA aims to empower students to thrive both during their studies and in their future public health careers. We aspire to be a dynamic force that supports our students' immediate needs and contributes to their long-term success and the broader public health discourse.

The Graduate Society of Women Engineers is a branch of the Society of Women Engineers UCI Chapter and aims to support the women in engineering graduate student community through social, professional, and personal development events and opportunities.
The purpose of the Organization is to provide a supportive and inclusive community for students to explore, practice, and grow in their Christian faith.

Haath is the Indian Fusion A Cappella team at UCI, that was created with the vision of perfectly blending the intricate heritage of Indian music with the sounds of contemporary Western tunes. We believe that A Cappella is not just about creating and performing mixes using only our voices, but is also about the opportunity for us to appreciate all the diversity and complexity of the music that surrounds us. Through our unique combinations of different languages, musical styles, and beats, we hope to enchant audiences by showcasing the power of storytelling and music.

Hack at UCI is an organization that reclaims the word hack back to its original meaning, to solve a problem creatively and effectively. Hack at UCI aims to cultivate a community of technical students at the University of California, Irvine. While other clubs may focus on expressive or computational parts of technology, Hack at UCI aims to enhance the practical and professional skills for students that may benefit (e.g. majors from the School of ICS, School of Engineering, and much more). Hack at UCI hosts two Hackathons, ZotHacks, and IrvineHacks, similar to those hosted at other UCs, that encourage students to build amazing technical projects. With a plethora of open source tools, community resources and events, and technical workshops, there is ample opportunity for anyone to bring their technical and professional goals to reality.

Hansori at UCI was formed in 2002 by four former students, who were inspired by Kim Duk Soo's Samulnori performance at the Barclay Theater. Since then, Hansori has been striving to spread Korean cultural awareness through the practice of traditional Korean drumming, known as Pungmul (풍물) and Samulnori (사물놀이). Hansori members learn and practice Korean percussion music that is performed by four traditional Korean instruments, representing four different weather components - thunder, rain, clouds, and wind. When played all together, they create “one sound”—the meaning of Hansori. Practices are held weekly throughout the school year to perform around Southern California with events including Lunar New Year celebrations, weddings, festivals, and many more.

Our mission is to harness the power of music to promote joy, healing, and community engagement.We are primarily a music therapy and community health organization, providing college studentsof all majors, regardless of musical background, with avenues to engage with and promotemusic, whether through performing, assisting with events, or supporting outreach initiatives.

club_name: Health and Justice Advocates at UCI
description: As public health students at the University of California, Irvine, we believe that we have a responsibility to support and take action regarding public policy decisions that impact the health and wellbeing of everyone globally from all communities. We believe that everyone deserves to live, work, study, and play in a healthy environment, to have access to good quality and affordable healthcare, and to live free from discrimination regardless of their race, ethnicity, gender, age, sexual orientation, disability or ability, religious affiliation, immigration status, or gender identity. This student group will engage in political advocacy efforts such as contacting state and national government representatives, starting petitions, letter, call, or email campaigns and attending events such as town halls in order to advocate around key public health issues including:● Discrimination against specific historically and contemporarily marginalized groups and its impact on health● Mental health, student wellness, and pedagogical wellness● Violence prevention, including firearms, injuries, and abuse among vulnerable populations● Access to reproductive and sexual health care services● Health and educational equity considerations from the COVID-19 pandemic● Health consequences (physical and mental) among undocumented immigrants and their families due to discrimination, lack of access to health care, and (threats of) deportation.

club_name: Hearts for the Homeless at UC Irvine
description: Hearts for the Homeless is a student-led nonprofit organization that provides free blood-pressure screening opportunities and heart health education to homeless populations around the United States and globally. H4H International is a team of undergraduate students, medical students, Ph.D. students, medical doctors, and other professionals who are invested in improving the well-being of homeless communities around the world, soon including Irvine.

HUME is an organization open for all students from schools such as UCLA and UCI. With a heart-centered on social responsibility, our mission revolves around enhancing the overall health and well-being of underserved communities located in the Middle East. As we believe in the power of unity and collaboration, we gather resources through our participating and local sponsors.

Her Campus, "A Collegiette's Guide to Life" Description: Her Campus is an online magazine for college women that individualizes its content college-by-college by establishing My Campus branches at schools across the country. With national content on Style, Health, Love, DormLife, and Career, supplemented by campus-specific content produced by teams of students at 60+ colleges across the country, Her Campus serves as a hub for everything college women need to know about today. Her Campus is written entirely by the nation's top college journalists. Since joining the Her Campus Team, our writers have been offered jobs and internships with the American Society of Magazine Editors (ASME) Intern Program and at Seventeen, Glamour, Teen Vogue, Marie Claire, InStyle, Harper\'s Bazaar, Hearst Digital Media Teen Network (Seventeen.com, CosmoGirl.com, DonateMyDress.org), O magazine, Reader\'s Digest, Details magazine, Us magazine, and Star magazine, among others. Founded by three students while they were undergraduates at Harvard: Stephanie Kaplan '10, Windsor Hanger '10, and Annie Wang '11. Her Campus was a winner in Harvard College's business plan competition, the i3 Innovation Challenge, in March 2009. Since Her Campus's launch in September 2009, Her Campus has formed content partnerships with Seventeen magazine and The Huffington Post and formed marketing partnerships with brands including New Balance, Juicy Couture, Rent the Runway, and Lauren Merkin. The site has been featured on ABC News Now, Fox25 News, CNN Money, AOL Money College, and in The Boston Globe, U.S. News & World Report, seventeen.com, Business Insider, The Boston Herald, The Metro, YPulse.com, Jezebel.com, and The Chronicle of Higher Education, among others. In July 2010, Stephanie, Windsor, and Annie were named to Inc. magazine\'s 30 Under 30 Coolest Young Entrepreneurs. HerCampus.com is the flagship website of Her Campus Media LLC. Her Campus Media LLC also owns HerCampusShop.com.
