Our Mission: - Define and provide a model for the future of online magazines by individualizing content - Fill the hole in the media marketplace for media that responds directly to the needs of college women - Serve as a career launching point for the nation\'s top college journalists by providing them with a national platform for the publication of their work - Connect companies with college students across the country in creative ways

The HER Health Initiative at UCI is committed to advancing and protecting female reproductive rights, believing that access to comprehensive and equitable reproductive healthcare is essential for achieving gender equality. Our mission is to create a welcoming space where women can come together to learn, share, and advocate for their own rights and the rights of women in our nation. Through our efforts, we aim to empower women with the knowledge, support, and confidence needed to advocate for reproductive rights for themselves and others.Our organization focuses on raising awareness of the critical issues surrounding reproductive justice and healthcare access. By hosting educational events, partnering with advocacy groups, and working with healthcare professionals, HER Health Initiative provides resources and learning opportunities to help our members become informed advocates. We emphasize the importance of understanding the broader social, economic, and political challenges that impact women’s health, striving to inspire action and dialogue within our campus and community.HER Health Initiative envisions a world where reproductive health is viewed as a right, not a privilege. Through our collective efforts, we strive to inspire a new generation of advocates who are ready to support one another, challenge inequalities, and work toward a future in which all women feel safe, informed, and empowered to make choices about their health. Together, we are building a foundation of understanding, compassion, and advocacy for the rights and well-being of women everywhere.

The Mission of this organization is to provide graduate and professional resources and leadership opportunities for predominantly Chicana/Latina college students and alumni. We achieve this by participating/implementing community service events, networking events, retention and recruitment initiatives, and academic and professional development workshops and events.

Hiking Club at UCI is a great opportunity to discover local trails alongside fellow UCI students with a common passion for hiking!We accept members of all skill levels. Hiking Club is more of an opportunity to make new friends and explore local trails!Socialize | Meet new peopleExercise | Avoid that freshman 15De-stress | Put aside stressful work

Hillel is an international organization throughout college campuses focused on fostering Jewish student involvment on campus. We provide a safe environment for students to join in fun activities and meet other Jewish students. Hillel welcomes all college students to come learn, teach, and experience different aspects of Judaism.

The purpose of Hindu YUVA at UCI is to bring together both Hindu and non-Hindu students to raise awareness about what Hinduism is. As one of the largest and oldest religions in the world, we believe it is necessary that there be an organization on campus to represent the interests of the Hindu community present here. We hope to create a comfortable atmosphere where students can come and celebrate the Hindu culture. We hope to achieve our mission by having team-building games, yoga and meditation, lively and exciting debates, and presentations at our weekly meetings. In other words, we want to build a small Hindu community within UCI so that students can come and discover a home away from home.

The Hmong Student Association at the University of California, Irvine is a revived student organization that strives to foster open communications between Hmong students, the Irvine community, and surrounding Hmong communities of Southern California. The organization strives to provide an atmosphere where students will be able to share and promote a deeper understanding of the Hmong culture towards one another and other students of the UCI community, promote higher education, and provide leadership and community service opportunities.

HoboBujo Club strives to create a relaxed, inclusive, non-judgmental, and safe environment for students to express themselves creatively in journals, mainly through physical media such as pens, pencils, markers, and paper, emphasizing that there is no right or wrong way to be creative.

Our mission at Hong Kong Student Union is to spread awareness of Hong Kong culture as well as to gather those who have interest in the culture. We are striving to expand our club by hosting cultural events which allow our students and club members to feel welcomed and included. The Hong Kong Student Union at UC Irvine targets our audience towards students who have a Hong Kong cultural background, however, we are open to anyone who has interest in learning more about our culture. Since Hong Kong is a relatively small place with a very unique culture, we hope to share this interesting culture with students at UC Irvine.We belong to U-852 organization which is made up of four UC schools to give more opportunities for our members and their members to share common cultures & interests. Beside connecting activities and cooperation with U852, we also have long-term partnerships with other student associations in UCI. In the global perspective, HKSU@UCI has also joined University of Hong Kong Student Association (UHKSA), which has 14 others top university, fostering partnerships and cooperating with them and aiming to create an interschool community in both the U.S and Hong Kong region. We hope that everyone is able to meet new friends, learn new things, and enjoy a good time while they are with us in UC Irvine!

club_name: Hospice Care Association at UC Irvine
description: Our mission is to educate students on the importance of understanding end-of-life care by incorporating the advocacies of Hospice care. We empower students to serve and grow through compassion, empathy, and emotional resilience by fostering a connected community to further serve those who need it most. Through involvement with local Hospice organizations, opportunities for career exploration, and guidance on how to become a Hospice volunteer, we hope to promote medical bereavement support by exploring a differing side of healthcare.

The Human Biology Club at UCI aims to provide students with guidance towards a career in medicine with an emphasis on community outreach and involvement. We will participate in local volunteering events and clinical opportunities. We hope to connect members to each other, alumni, medical students, and health professionals. Additionally, our mentorship will provide our members with an understanding of how to achieve their academic goals. The Human Biology Club is not restricted to the major and welcomes anyone with an interest in human biology and medicine.

club_name: Human Resources Management Association at UCI
description: Our organization aims to educate young professionals on the nuances within the HR industry through guest speakers, mentorship and internship programs, professional workshops, and certification opportunities.

The Ice Hockey Club at UCI plays ice hockey on a recreational and a competitive level with the American Collegiate Hockey Association division 3 in the West Coast Hockey Conference tier 2. Our objectives is to build a network amongst people with similar interests, advancing social and communication skills, organizing and participating in competitions on a collegiate level, and improving Ice Hockey techniques through instruction and mentorship.

To improve student life of the Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences academically, socially, and professionally by creating and deepening the bonds between students, faculty, administration, companies, and alumni of the ICS School as well as similar groups outside of the Information and Computer Sciences.

club_name: If/When/How: Lawyering for Reproductive Justice at UCI Law
description: If/When/How: Lawyering for Reproductive Justice at UCI is a chapter of the national If/When/How organization whose mission is to train and mobilize law students and lawyers across the country to foster legal expertise and support for the realization of reproductive justice. We believe that individuals enjoy reproductive justice when they can each choose if, when, and how to create and sustain a family. Our chapter is focused on contributing to achieving this goal through sponsoring speaker panels on reproductive justice issues, getting students involved in lobbying and pro bono work, and continuing to fight for the preservation of reproductive rights in defiance of the Supreme Court's decision in Dobbs v. Jackson Women's Health Organization.

Our name stands for "International Medicine, Education, and Development" and we are the chapter of a national organization at UC Irvine , the Foundation for the International Medical Relief of Children (FIMRC). Our mission is to increase medical care access and disease prevention for under-served and underprivileged children both locally and abroad. IMED is a community service project organization which hosts a variety of events both locally and internationally. Our main current projects are: the Health Smart Project (health education in after school programs), the Orphanage Project (hosted primarily in Tijuana, Mexico), the Mentorship Project (healthcare physicians mentoring), the Outreach Project and the Global Actions Project (medical mission abroad). Health Smart allows our members to go to local after school programs to educate youth of various ages about staying healthy and proactive about their well-being. Orphanage Project works closely with an orphanage in Tijuana, Mexico where we spend a day with the children to teach them about health measures and science materials. The Outreach Project works with a nonprofit organization called Spirit League to help kids with disabilities to play sports; this project also works with Los Alamitos Lestonnac Free Clinic to allow members to gain regular volunteer hours and help an underserved community. Global Actions gives members an opportunity to travel around the world to learn about other culture's medical practices, volunteer at clinics in the Dominican Republic, Peru, India, Panama, Philippines and many other countries. Mentorship is a chance for members to gain one on one interaction with health professionals of their choice and gain valuable insight into the life of a health professional. Along with these five projects, IMED brings out special guest speakers throughout the year to learn about all the different possibilities of careers in the health care field. IMED is a pre-health club which encourages all majors to come check us out!

IDC at UCI aims to promote and celebrate the art of dance, with a specific focus on Jazz, K-pop, and Hip-hop genres. The organization's mission is to provide a supportive and creative community for all UCI students interested in dancing, allowing them to exchange skills, learn from each other, and experience the joy of dancing together. IDC at UCI strives to create a welcoming and inclusive environment that fosters personal growth, friendship, and cultural exchange through the art of dance.

Improv Revolution generates creativity, comedy, and community at and around UC Irvine. Through a positive approach to improvisation, we create opportunities for as many people as possible to engage in the community and grow their confidence on stage. We strive to create smart, unifying comedy that is accessible by all. Our core team auditions quarterly, meets weekly, and performs biweekly. We encourage you to come audition! We also offer free workshops, no audition or experience required, on campus every Friday! Anyone is eligible to drop by. Check out our website at www.improvrevolution.org, give us a follow on our Instagram, Twitter, and Facebook pages, @improvrevolution and @irevuci respectively, to stay updated on our workshops, auditions, and performances!
We empower students to promote sustainable and responsible business.

club_name: Indian Classical Music Club at UCI
description: ICM@UCI's mission is to provide a recurring space for the growth of a vibrant, passionate community of Indian Classical Musicians and Artists at UCI. Through that space, we aspire to collectively bring out the creative and spiritual beauty of the rich Indian Classical Music tradition, furthering our own individual musical journeys, spiritual growth, and ultimately, our lives. As we develop, we maintain the bold aim to spread awareness and appreciation of this beautiful art form across the UCI campus, engaging in public performances to spread the richness of the Indian Classical Arts beyond its traditional audience.

The Indian Sub-continental Club (ISC) at University of California, Irvine has been an influential and active student organization for over two decades. The goal of ISC is to unite the students of UC Irvine whose cultural roots come from that of the Indian Sub-continent: Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, the Maldives, Nepal, Pakistan, and Sri Lanka. Every year ISC holds numerous activities to spread cultural awareness and provide a place where students from similar backgrounds can meet and interact. It also provides an environment to stimulate cultural awareness through various ISC-sponsored activities and events, such as our Culture Show, Diwali celebration, and Holi.

We are the Indonesian Students at UC Irvine (ISUCI) and we continually strive to create an inclusive social platform for fellow Indonesian students at the University of California, Irvine. Through our numerous events and networking opportunities, we aim to welcome, guide and grow our members while celebrating the diverse Indonesian culture here in Irvine.

The Industry Pharmacy Organization at UCI is dedicated to advancing the careers of industry pharmacists. IPhO at UCI accomplishes this by providing timely and relevant information that is vital to our members. IPhO at UCI also raises awareness among employers and industry executives about the role that industry pharmacists can play in drug development and appropriate medication use. IPhO at UCI provides targeted resources and coaching to enhance members' continuing education and professional development. IPhO at UCI is also critical in creating opportunities for members to network and exchange ideas with their industry pharmacist peers.

InfrasCtrl at UCI empowers underrepresented, small, and student-run businesses through technology. Our mission is to design and develop free websites that help entrepreneurs build legitimacy, increase visibility, and access financial opportunities such as grants and loans. By combining website design, social media outreach, and community collaboration, we aim to bridge the digital divide and promote equitable access to digital tools.

INSA dance is an exhibition open choreography dance team based at UC Irvine. Founded in 2008, our mission is to share our passion and love for dance with the public. As a family, we uphold our values and the name, I Never Stand Alone.

club_name: Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers at UCI - IEEE
description: IEEE at UCI is a premier engineering club working at the intersection of electrical engineering, computer engineering, and computer science. We provide a place for those who are interested in both hardware and software to consistently meet and develop their skills and passions with others. There are three ways we do this: The first is our lab and community room at ICS 225, and it is open every day. The second is the OPS Program (Open Project Space), a year-long extracurricular program designed to teach programming and embedded electronics to eager and willing students, supporting them every step of the way.Lastly, we serve as the gateway to lifelong membership and community with the greater IEEE community from IEEE Orange County, IEEE Region 6, and IEEE International. Our mission is to ensure those who come to us have a good time, learn a lot, and find IEEE a place they can belong to for life.

The Institute of Transportation Engineers is an international educational and scientific association of transportation professionals who are responsible for meeting mobility and safety needs. ITE facilitates the application of technology and scientific principles to research, planning, functional design, implementation, operation, policy development and management for any mode of ground transportation. Through its products and services, ITE promotes professional development of its members, supports and encourages education, stimulates research, develops public awareness programs and serves as a conduit for the exchange of professional information.

The Intellectual Property Law Society (IPLS) is dedicated to exploring and promoting academic, professional, and industry issues at the intersection of law and intellectual property—including copyright, trademark, patent, trade secret, and related fields. Through engagement with legal professionals, faculty, and peers, IPLS fosters a dynamic and supportive community for students passionate about intellectual property law.

Our mission is to teach students of underserved K-12 Title 1 schools in the Orange County area about Neuroscience and STEM topics. We share our enthusiasm for the brain through our unique lessons and demonstrations. We travel to elementary schools, middle schools, and high schools in disadvantaged areas of Orange County to work with students at schools receiving poor funding in the sciences. Our long term goal is to create and foster interest, excitement, and curiosity about the brain.In addition to visiting K-12 students and hosting events on UCI’s campus, InterAxon prides itself on being an all-inclusive, welcoming organization where anyone interested in science and service can join, regardless of major or year. We truly are one big family and we hope you can join us to meet and make life-long friends along the way!

The Interfraternity Council (IFC) serves as the self-governing body for the fraternities at the University of California Irvine. It consists of the Executive Board and the Council. The executive board consists of fraternity members who are elected into their positions by the IFC Council. The Council consists of presidents and delegates from each chapter. Every Monday of the academic year the executive board and council convene for formal IFC meeting at 11 am in the Dr. White Room in the Cross-Cultural Center.

The International Law Forum at the University of California, Irvine seeks to foster an engaged community of students passionate about global governance, law, and justice. Our mission is to promote scholarly dialogue and collaboration on issues of international law, politics, and policy by providing students with a platform to research, publish, and debate emerging global legal challenges. Through open discussion, educational programming, and interaction with policymakers and practitioners, we aim to cultivate critical thinking, cross-cultural understanding, and professional development for the next generation of global leaders.

club_name: International Law Society at UCI - ILS
description: The International Law Society (ILS) at UCI is a forum for discussing topics in international law. ILS seeks to contribute to the academic dialogue at UCI and among other law schools through collaborative events, clinical work, and a supportive curriculum.

ISG is an official Christian student group at UC Irvine. We welcome all students: undergraduate and graduate, Christian and non-Christian, and especially international students. The students in our group come from many countries around the world, including the United States. Our mission is to "love locally, impact globally," in which we seek to create a "home away from home" for students studying in Irvine. We offer weekly Bible studies, as well as special talks and lectures on topics such as the relationship between Science and Faith, evidence for the existence of God, the problem of suffering, and others. We also offer English classes, small group gatherings, fun trips around the SoCal area.

club_name: International Student Mentorship Program at UCI
description: The purpose of this organization shall be to support international students to thrive during their studies and equip them with life and leadership skills needed to be successful beyond graduation. This is accomplished through mentorship with professional volunteers, workshops led by experienced industry professionals, English conversation sessions, and relationship-building events that help students navigate academic life, cultural adjustment, and career transitions while building a supportive community.
We are a student-led movement committed to actively pursuing Jesus Christ as a witnessing community.

Iranian Student Union is a campus organization at the University of California, Irvine. ISU hopes to unify Iranian students of UC Irvine in order to form an educational and social environment where Iranians can embrace their culture and history. With UCI located in the most heavily populated Persian community outside of Iran, we hope to spread awareness of our traditions through cultural and social events. Our group aims to bring together Iranian-Americans and non-Iranians alike, to celebrate and embrace our lavish heritage while promoting a strong sense of identity and community. We host many culture nights, charity events, and fundraisers throughout the year, culminating in our annual culture show.

The Iraqi Student Association serves as a home for all students to connectand share the rich heritage of Iraq. Our mission is to foster a unified, inclusive environmentthat celebrates the beauty and diversity of Iraqi culture.

Hello! We're the Irvine Chess Club. Join us to meet and play with fellow chess players from UCI! Beginners, intermediate players, and experts are all welcome. Feel free to check out our discord where we post club announcements, host tournaments, and play/discuss chess: https://discord.gg/dbHGrZYxBp

At Irvine Consulting Group, we are a dynamic team of driven andinnovative students from UC Irvine, united by a shared commitment to bridging the gapbetween academic knowledge and real-world impact. Founded on the vision of makingconsulting accessible to all, ICG provides hands-on client engagements, resources,and professional development opportunities to help students excel in consulting andbeyond.
The Irvine Hacker Fab is an interdisciplinary engineering student organization aiming to democratize access to semiconductor fabrication through the development of open-source tools and software.

Our mission at Irvine Investment and Trading Group (Irvine ITG) is to empower students with the technical capacities necessary for success in the financial industry. We strive to provide a comprehensive and practical learning experience, tailored to the needs of our members, that will prepare them for their personal and professional ambitions.With a focus on real-world applications and industry-specific knowledge, our development program and specialized sessions offer a unique opportunity to broaden perspectives and deepen understanding of finance as a whole. Through networking events and an inclusive community, we aim to inspire and support our members on their journey to becoming leaders in the financial sector.

Ivy Sound at UCI is a music-based organization open to all students who are passionate about any aspect of the music industry—whether they aspire to be producers, artists, managers, marketers, audio engineers, music lawyers, or entrepreneurs. Our purpose is to create a space where creativity, collaboration, and ambition come together to help students turn their ideas into reality within the music industry.We aim to empower students to think entrepreneurially, explore their artistic and business potential, and gain hands-on experience that connects them to real opportunities in the music world. Through workshops, showcases, collaborative projects, and social events, Ivy Sound builds a vibrant community where members can grow their skills, form valuable relationships, and have fun in the process.In the short term, our goal is to establish a strong creative network on campus that brings together musically minded students from all majors and backgrounds. In the long term, Ivy Sound seeks to become the central hub for student-driven music innovation at UCI—bridging the gap between campus creators and the larger entertainment industry.

J-Fashion Club at UCI is a student-run organization that welcomes undergraduate and graduate students to participate and learn about a variety of different Japanese fashion subcultures. Jfashion Club’s goal is to create a safe space for individuals of all genders, racial, and geographic backgrounds to feel comfortable with freely expressing who they are through makeup and fashion.

The Japanese Student Association at UCI is a multicultural social club dedicated to the exchange of Japanese and American cultures. Here, students have the opportunity to make new intercollegiate friends, celebrate the extensive world of Japanese culture, and even access career opportunities in Japan.

The Jazz Co-lab Club at University of California, Irvine (UCI) is dedicated to cultivating a vibrant and inclusive community of dancers and musicians from all majors. Our mission is to foster the art of improvisational jazz dance, nurturing creativity, and igniting the joy of movement among our members. With the dedication and passion of our team, the club envisions becoming a prominent force for artistic expression, creativity, and community engagement within UCI. Our aspiration is to both inspire and be inspired, creating a legacy of rhythm, movement, and unity that transcends boundaries and enriches the lives of all who embark on this dance journey.Together, we dance to the symphony of spontaneity, forging bonds and moving harmoniously towards a future where the echoes of improvisational jazz music resonate through generations. While the concept of live music paired with live dance is as ancient as time itself, the notion of "jazz" took root in the nourishing embrace of the African diaspora. This communal evolution found its initial resonance in the vibrant spaces of New Orleans and Harlem during the 1920s, embodied by the likes of Whitey's Lindy Hoppers and Chick Webb's Orchestra.

JHOP is the contending House of Prayer for the UCI campus and the city of Irvine. We believe that prayer is key to seeing God move in our personal lives and our community. Further, in prayer, we receive God's heart for our community and the grace to be His light and love to those around us. We can't do anything apart from God, and through prayer, we learn to abide in and partner with Him. Our long-term vision is to establish a 24-7 house of prayer and worship in Irvine from which evangelism and outreach will flow.

MISSION STATEMENT The Jewish Law Association (JLA) is dedicated to: -Facilitating meaningful connections between Jewish law students -Organizing events for the benefit of the membership and the law school community as a whole -Fostering outreach with the Orange County Jewish legal community -Exploring the unique legal and cultural aspects of Judaism -Providing opportunities for tikkun olam (social action) Membership is open to all current law students, regardless of individual religious affiliation.

Jodaiko is a collegiate taiko group from the main campus of the University of California, Irvine. Now in its 34th year since inception, Jodaiko brings the Japanese art of taiko to UCI and the rest of Southern California. The word "Jodaiko" means "passionate drumming" in Japanese, and as a collegiate taiko group, each member must balance their passion for taiko with their desire to pursue an education. Jodaiko takes pride in the diverse cultures, areas of study, and performance experiences each member represents.

Our mission is to promote the art of Judo by fostering physical fitness, mental discipline, andcamaraderie, while cultivating respect, resilience, and continuous personal growth within asupportive university community.

Jugger at UCI exists to provide a space in which UCI students can learn, teach, play, and participate in the sport known as “Jugger”. This space is meant to form a long-term community in the Irvine area around the sport jugger, as well as providing a new space for socialization and team building. Jugger at UCI will engage in community outreach to foster engagement and engage students for tournaments and events held around the U.S.

Kaba Modern is a collegiate dance group founded in 1992 by Arnel Calvario. As a proud part of the Filipino-American club, Kababayan, he established the group to perform in various events, such as Philipino Cultural Night and others. As Kaba Modern enters its thirtieth season, we hope to become an official organization on UCI's campus in order to connect with students as well as others in the community. "We are a family of creatives existing to foster a safe and inclusive space for artistic expression, interpersonal connection, & self-discovery. Through collective artistry, dance education, & enriching events, we aim to bridge and positively impact diverse communities, honor the history and heritage of the art forms we practice, & promote intentional movement."

Kababayan at UCI promotes awareness and enrichment of the Pilipinx/Pilipinx-American culture, tradition and heritage. As a student organization, Kababayan emphasizes the social, cultural, political, academic and community aspects of the Pilipinx/Pilipinx-American experience.
Achievement in Every Field of Human Endeavor

Yesterday, today, and tomorrow, Kappa Alpha Theta exists to nurture each member throughout her college and alumnae experience and to offer a lifelong opportunity for social, intellectual and moral growth as she meets the higher and broader demands of mature life.

The Fraternity should complement and enhance the educational mission of the University of California, Irvine. It is committed to fostering a close cooperative partnership with our school. The Fraternity should promote academic achievement and assist each member in achieving his academic potential. By helping members adjust to the college environment, it helps them pursue their degree goals. Co-curricular activities are valuable alongside classroom experience, so the Fraternity encourages involvement in all aspects of campus life.The Fraternity promotes the ideal of Brotherhood. Creating lifelong friendships is a primary benefit of membership. It fulfills the need to belong to an extended family and often strengthens those personal relationships through shared living situations. Members are expected to care about the welfare of their brothers. Brotherhood is a lifetime commitment, and strong alumni-undergraduate relationships are encouraged for the benefit of both groups.
Help others how you wish you were helped.

Kendo Club at UCI practices the traditional martial art of Kendo: one which practitioners use a wooden sword to strike others. Here, students learn, train, and compete with others at intercollegiate tournaments. Kendo club aims to train body, mind, and character through the way of the sword.

Û╣Ø KKAP K-pop Dance Team, or KKAP, is a dance team composed of a diverse group of people who share a mutual love for K-pop. We strive to create an inclusive and encouraging space where dancers of all levels can learn and express their passion for K-pop through dance.

Klesis is a Christian club at UC Irvine. Klesis welcomes those with a church background as well as people simply interested in talking about spiritual topics, as we believe that college is perfect time to investigate the bigger questions of life and the Christian worldview, and to discover who God is and who He calls us to be. We're also pros when it comes to food, mentorship, growth opportunities, and discipleship. We also love having fun and developing close friendships that can last a lifetime.

The Korean American Student Association at University of California Irvine promotes student involvement in the social, academic, political, and community service aspects of the Korean American community. Our goal is to create a friendly, comfortable, and educational environment for Korean American students.

Korean Health Association (KHA) was established back in 1986 for both international and American students at the University of California, Irvine, to serve the following purposes: (1) Offer assistance and consultation to students regarding their future education/career goals. (2) Enable students to help one another reach their education/career goals through various academic and emotional support. (3) Assist students in achieving successful academic endeavors in undergraduate studies. (4) Encourage peer counseling and tutoring among students. (5) Enable students to meet one another. Although KHA concentrates on the members' academic concerns, it also provides opportunities for them to develop life-lasting friendships.
To provide, in the areas of science, technology and entrepreneurship, opportunities for:- International Cooperation- Career Development- Community Service

club_name: Kristos Campus Missions (formerly Korean-American Campus Mission)
description: A Christian ministry to show the love of Christ on UCI and to the ends of the world. To obey the Great Commission by discipling and mobilizing collegians.

The purpose of this organization is to increase the retention and graduation rate of the Latine community at UCI, provide a safe space to unpack cultural stigmas and traumas, as well as provide resources to help navigate UCI. This will be achieved through Our Valores: [Goodness], Cultural celebration, and Our Stories. The above-mentioned shall serve as the foundational core values that La Familia will abide by to create a home-away-from-home and create an environment for students to create a chosen family in this new home. This will consist of creating a space of support on campus and a memorable salient time with an emphasis on breaking down stereotypes and prejudices associated with being a person of Latine origin. As we build a home, we strive to address the adversities and hardships from college experiences that Latine face, which this organization will push Latine to work for. This organization will provide resources and reach out to the Hispanic/Latine community. We will serve as an avenue for networking and providing members with enrichment in academics, community service, and social networking-initiated, events, fundraisers, debates/discussions, and functions that have been voted for and or will be voted for by club members during an official club meeting. This will be achieved through Our Valores: Community, Cultural Celebration, and Our Stories. The above-mentioned shall serve as the foundational core values that La Familia will abide by to create a home-away-from-home and create an environment for students to create a chosen family in this new home

club_name: La Unidad Latina, Lambda Upsilon Lambda Fraternity, Inc.
description: La Unidad Latina, Lambda Upsilon Lambda Fraternity, Incorporated primarily seeks to take a leadership role in meeting the needs of the Latino community through academic achievement, cultural awareness, community service and promotion of the Latino culture and people.

The purpose of the Labor and Work Law Society is to educate members in labor and employment law, as well as the attorney and advocate's role in furthering the advancement of workers' rights nationally and globally; to provide plaintiff and management-side networking opportunities to members; and to engage in solidarity through action to advocate for the dignity of all workers.

Founded at UCI, Lambda Phi Nu is a co-ed business leadership fraternity dedicated to igniting leaders, illuminating communities, and inspiring legacies on and off campus. Our fraternity helps individuals develop an excellent sense of professionalism and social responsibility while upholding high standards of academic excellence. We strive to guide our members toward success in their careers and build upon their commitment to bettering their community. We aim to create an environment for students to develop their leadership potential, grow their understanding of various industries and pathways, and accomplish their goals. At the intersection of business and brotherhood, Lambda Phi Nu cultivates a community for students to be and belong.

Lambda Theta Delta is the only officially recognized Asian American interest fraternity at the University of California Irvine. Founded on March 2, 1983, Lambda Theta Delta is the first and largest Asian-American interest fraternity at UCI.Since its inception at the University of California, Irvine over three decades ago, Lambda Theta Delta has initiated over 1000 members and has become one of the most influential local student organizations in Southern California.Although Lambda Theta Delta is an Asian American fraternity, individuals from all ethnic backgrounds are welcome to join. LTD stays true to its roots by continuing to promote Asian American interests and giving back to the community, while maintaining the strongest and most diverse brotherhood that simply cannot be paralleled.

club_name: Land Use and Real Estate Law Society
description: The Land Use and Real Estate Society is dedicated to fostering a dynamic and inclusive environment for students interested in the legal frameworks that shape real estate law, real estate development, and land use regulation. Through speaker events, networking sessions, and career-focused workshops, we expose students to the diverse pathways available within real estate law—from transactional work and litigation to zoning and urban planning. Our mission is to equip future attorneys with the knowledge, connections, and confidence to thrive in a complex and evolving legal landscape.

club_name: Language and Linguistics Club (formerly Syntax PROs)
description: The mission of Language and Linguistics Club is to expose members of the UC Irvine community to the beauty and science of language and its interactions with culture and history. We seek to create an open space for students to discuss any topics in the field of linguistics, from their social impacts to the underlying syntactic structures. The events associated with our club will emphasize linguistic and cultural diversity as well as an increased awareness of the underlying grammatical structures and features of languages other than English.

club_name: Latina Empowerment and Development at UCI
description: Our mission is to empower Latina students and their allies at UCI by connecting them with professional, academic, and leadership opportunities through the Harvard Latina Empowerment and Development (LEAD) network. Our goals include promoting mentorship, access to internships, leadership development, and participation in the annual LEAD Conference hosted at Harvard University. Through these efforts, the LEAD Chapter at UCI aims to create a lasting impact on campus by equipping students with the tools, connections, and confidence to lead and succeed in their chosen fields, while embodying the values of empowerment, education, and community.

club_name: Latines In Pharmaceutical Sciences at UCI
description: LIPS at UCI will change lives by offering a space and community where Hispanic and other underrepresented/marginalized groups can express themselves and develop leadership and technical skills through opportunities and community support.

The Latino Business Student Association is a student-run non-profit organization established in 2003. The purpose of LBSA is to assist its members from various ethnic backgrounds and fields of studies at UCI, to pursue professional skills and careers while raising awareness of the Latinx culture. The organization accomplishes this by focusing on its three pillars: Professional Development, Social Interaction, and Community Service, with a foundation on Academic Achievement.
LMSA recruits and supports individuals in healthcare professions who will strive to improve access to and delivery of healthcare to Latin@s and medically underserved populations.

The Latinx Law Students Association (LLSA) at UCI Law is an all-inclusive organization that is open to any student, regardless of racial or ethnic identification. As law students at the only public law school in Orange County, an area in which the largest ethnic minority group is Latinx, we believe it is particularly important to address the many issues that affect Latinx people at both an institutional level and in the community. Our mission is to confront these issues through community service, mentorship, coalition building, and networking.

The Latinx Student Psychological Association (LSPA) is committed to providing a multifaceted awareness of both professional and educational resources to enhance the college experiences of dedicated students aspiring to serve underrepresented communities in the mental health arena. **LSPA is open to all majors and racial/ethnic backgrounds** LSPA's Mission is to: Part 1. To facilitate the professional and career development of aspiring psychologists and other service providers who desire an education beyond the baccalaureate degree. Part 2. To assist undergraduates to develop a sense of community, highlighting the value of serving the Latina/o communities and other underserved groups. Part 3. To promote students' educational experiences and expand multicultural awareness and training in the field of psychology. Part 4. To build a connection between undergraduate students, faculty/ staff, and community leaders, establishing a strong social network, both on and off campus. Philosophy: The association will emphasize the value of academics, research, practical experience, leadership, and community service for a complete undergraduate experience. In addition, the cabinet recognizes the value of the five elements for the successful application of graduate school. Through programming, dialogues, workshops and other educational activities, LSPA aspires to assist students to acquire a comprehensive education while attending to the five pillars throughout their experience at UC Irvine.

club_name: Law Students for Educational Equity at UCI Law
description: LSEE aims to expose law students interested in practicing education law or becoming law school professors/administrators to the necessary resources to succeed.

club_name: Law Students for Justice in Palestine
description: The purpose of this organization shall be to serve as a hub, on UCI Law’s campus, for education, discussion, and activism in support of the Palestinian right to self-determination, justice, and equality.

club_name: League of United Latin American Citizens (LULAC) at UCI
description: The Mission of the League of United Latin American Citizens at UCI is to advance the economic condition, educational attainment, political influence, housing, health and civil rights of the Hispanic population of the United States.

The goal of this club is to: A. To promote the interests of the Lebanese and non-Lebanese students at UC Irvine. B. To acquaint the UCI community with Lebanon and the Lebanese people, and to promote their culture. C. To help Lebanese students integrate better into the diverse UCI community by creating an atmosphere of friendship & support. D. To form a closely knit community on campus.

club_name: Leukemia and Lymphoma Society at UCI
description: The Leukemia and Lymphoma Society at UCI is a national organization dedicated to curing leukemia, lymphoma, Hodgkin’s disease and myeloma, and improving the quality of life of patients and their families. LLS at UCI’s mission is to provide a forum for discussion, education, awareness, funding, and support of our shared interest in making an impact in the fight against blood cancer. As well as to provide a place to participate in various interactions such as; service, advocacy efforts, education, fundraising and facilitating events tailored to our organizational interests.

Level V Origins is an exhibition dance team that exists to provide the opportunity for those who have never had previous dance experience to explore different forms of dance. Our goal is to develop and hone leadership skills through our shared passion for dance.

Our mission is to introduce the fundamentals of coding and programming to students and provide them with hands-on learning, as well as industry experience for the more advanced coders. With the vast library of online LikeLion lectures, we are planning to provide lessons on various fields of coding, including python, java, and UI-UX and general front-end coding. For the members with prior coding background, we will push them to develop projects in a real-world settings to prepare them for the tech industry.

club_name: Live Action at UCI (formerly Anteaters For Life)
description: The purpose of Live Action at UCI will be to defend the rights of the most vulnerable in society. The short term goals will be to engage all UCI students with a passion for advocating for life, and to educate students that all life is valuable and needs to be protected from the moment of conception. We aim to make sure the womb remains the safest place anyone could be. The long term goals will be to continue to provide opportunities and resources for all UCI students interested in respectfully engaging in advocating for the lives of the unborn.

At Living Stone Christian Fellowship, Cantonese is our heart language: LSFers come from wherever Cantonese is spoken! Each year of LSF has a different flavor, contributed by each person's unique story, gifts, pain, brokenness, and dreams. But our focus on Jesus remains the same. We envision LSF to be a safe space for college students (including seekers with questions about faith) to grow in identity, character, and life purpose via experiencing Christ-centered community.

Living Water College Ministry is a Mandarin college ministry that exists to love God and love people. Our mission is to share the Gospel and to grow relationships in God and fellowship. We desire to learn and study the Word through Bible study, sermon discussion, and prayer.

Made with Love focuses on organizing craft-based activities in order to give meaningful donations back to the community. We are not only passionate about crafting but also being able to craft with a purpose! We strive to promote self-compassion and compassion for others, while at the same time, bringing awareness to certain issues that have an impact in our own community.

club_name: MAES Latinos in Science and Engineering
description: To encourage Latinos in STEM and promote unity while developing them as better students, leaders, and professionals.
Mission Statement: To foster a community where magic can be taught, learned, and discovered.

club_name: Magic The Gathering Club at UCI
description: Students who meet to enjoy their mutual love of the Magic: the Gathering card game.We meet in the West Food Court on Tuesdays and Thursdays from 6-10 pm.Make sure to check out our discord (https://www.discord.gg/XMtau5Xu2A) to get the latest information on the club.

club_name: Management Information Student Society at UCI - MAISS
description: Management Information Student Society's mission revolves around strengthening the business and technology community at UC Irvine. They are an organization with a tight-knit community of students who focus on building themselves professionally. In addition to having a mentorship program and going on retreats, they also code, apply to internships, and get food together! The way that MAISS differentiates itself from other organizations on campus is by having business and tech-related workshops such as intro to SQL/Product Management and tech/non-tech recruitment, and company events from Zillow, Twitter, Visa, and more!

The purpose of Manifest is to create a community of success and result-driven entrepreneurs by focusing on fostering business education among the members. The organization further aims to encourage start-up building by spreading the right entrepreneurial mindset and the motivation to solve real-life market problems by leveraging each other's competencies and sharing of skills.
MODUCI empowers musicians to continue to show their mexican heritage through Mariachi music fostering appreciation and understanding of cultures within our campus community.
Mariners at UCI exists to see college-aged students fearlessly change the world.

Established in 2013, the Marketing Association has dedicated itself towards developing the marketing community at the University of California, Irvine. Our diverse and growing organization welcomes Anteaters from all majors and academic levels with a passion or interest in marketing. Together, we aspire to become the forefront of the undergraduate marketing community on campus and in Orange County.

MatSci@UCI is an academic resource that offers information and networking opportunities to students, who are working, studying, or interested in the field of Materials Science. We provide information about the broad application of Materials Science through detailed presentation in the various fields of engineering and industry. With the participation of upperclassmen, guest speakers, and faculty, we provide a social environment for students to network and utilize their academic resources at UC Irvine.

club_name: Math Finance Club at UCI - MFC
description: This organization strives to recruit highly quantitative students across campus with the purpose of fostering an interest in Finance and providing a medium for members to navigate their way into the industry.
A Math students federation provides Lower Level Math courses review session and activities.

As the UCI branch of M.E.M.O. (Medical, Educational Missions and Outreach), a 501(c)(3) non-profit, student-run, humanitarian organization that seeks to serve the underprivileged by addressing their medical and educational needs, we raise money and medical supplies to send back to Vietnam. As a whole organization, we are composed of volunteers, students, physicians, and other health professionals. Of the group of volunteers, students from UCI have the opportunity to travel to Vietnam to witness the beautiful impact our help provides. At UCI, M.E.M.O.’s primary goal is to provide medical care and educational opportunities to the underserved in Vietnam and the local community of Southern California. By supplying the underserved with the fundamental needs (health and education) deprived of them by poverty, M.E.M.O. hopes to give them a foundation in which they can raise themselves out of their current living conditions. M.E.M.O. also aims to spread awareness of the abject poverty seen in third world countries to the younger generation in the U.S. to propagate the notion of social responsibility into a brighter future.

MÈO aims to enhance access to healthcare within Limited English Proficiency (LEP) Asian communities in the Orange County area. Asian-American communities face unique challenges in accessing healthcare due to their diverse ethnic groups, cultures. With the largest Vietnamese population outside of Vietnam, Orange County has a significant need for culturally and linguistically proficient liaisons to reduce the barriers faced by this community.

club_name: Medical Experience Though Service in Healthcare
description: MESH at UCI is a student-run organization dedicated to supporting non-profit health clinics in optimizing their services while providing students with the opportunity to gain firsthand exposure to various aspects of the medical field as they pursue careers in healthcare. In addition, MESH collaborates with a range of healthcare-focused non-profit organizations to improve access and resources for underserved communities. The organization seeks to serve as a bridge between understaffed free clinics and UCI students eager to volunteer, while extending its support to non-profit health organizations both locally and globally. By encouraging student participation in health-related service activities, MESH works to raise awareness of the healthcare needs of low-income communities and to equip its members with the leadership and professional experience necessary to make a meaningful impact.
Medical Marvels at UC Irvine is a chapter of the international pre-health nonprofit Medical Marvels that offers students a community for professional growth and medical exposure.

Medics in Armenia is a student organization at UCI. It is meant to educate and train students that are interested and/or are pursing a future in medicine by traveling to Armenia to shadow medical professionals and volunteer at impoverished communities across Armenia. This organization also hopes to guide students in establishing significant connections with those in the medical field by holding meetings throughout the school year with guest speakers such as medical professionals.

MEDLIFE strives to deliver aid to local communities as well as provide for communities abroad in underdeveloped countries including Peru, Ecuador, Tanzania and others that are in dire need of medical aid. With the help of volunteers and MEDLIFE Mobile Clinics, we can deliver primary care services to individuals and families who otherwise lack access, as MEDLIFE believes that access to quality healthcare is a basic human right. MEDLIFE @ UC Irvine plans to give back not only to the local community, but also to international communities in need through volunteer-based service trips.

MedTech at UCI is dedicated to advancing innovation at the intersection of cognitive science and biomedical research through the development of customized software solutions. Our mission is to empower students to apply artificial intelligence, machine learning, cloud and gamification approaches to real-world challenges in healthcare and neuroscience.Through collaborative software development, we aim to support research efforts in cognitive science and medicine. By integrating clinical, behavioral, and physiological data, our projects contribute to the creation and maintenance of intelligent systems that enable personalized care and accelerate scientific discovery.We provide members with hands-on experience through mentorship, team-based projects, and exposure to real-world industry practices. Our goal is to foster a close-knit community of interdisciplinary thinkers and developers who are passionate about shaping the future of healthcare and cognitive science through meaningful, ethical, and impactful technology.

The men's club volleyball team at UCI consists of athletes who are passionate about the sport and seek to compete at a high level. We hold our members to high expectations and full commitment as our goal is to represent UCI with honor and pride. The team competes in the SCCVL and other tournaments around the country. We also aim to provide a competitive environment for men to learn and grow in the sport of volleyball, build a brotherhood and friendships that are sustained on and off the court, maintain the legacy that had been established by dedicated members of this program, and compete at the highest level for this sport and hold each other accountable.

club_name: Men's Club Water Polo at UCI
description: Water polo is a competitive sport in which a team uses their athletic, cognitive, and collaborative skills to beat out their competition. The Men's Club Water Polo at UCI is dedicated to playing a smarter and stronger game. We welcome any dedicated player who wishes to continue their polo career past high school. We are a club that will have fun playing the game we love while working hard and meeting a group of interesting and fun people. New players are always welcome as well!

Men's Lacrosse Club at UCI is the official Club lacrosse team for the campus. We compete in the Men's Collegiate Lacrosse Association or MCLA. We are a part of the associations Southern Lacrosse Conference which is arguably the most competitive conference in the association. We compete against a range of teams such as Long Beach, UCSD and even the Mexico National team. We were even picked to host the MCLA quarter final championships for 2015! If you are interested in becoming a part of our team visit our website or send us an Email.

Men's Rowing Club at UCI is a competitive rowing team that trains year long for its sprint season in the spring. Each year, the crew travels to compete with some of the best crews in the nation and internationally. Aside from building nationally competitive athletes, we strive to create outstanding and successful students.

The club serves as an opportunity for students to compete at a competitive level representing UCI in US College Club Soccer whilst being able to participate in the campus academic atmosphere to the greatest extent they are so inclined. Furthermore, the club seeks to foster a sense of brotherhood within the team, in order to allow the members to reach greater collective and personal goals.

club_name: Men's Ultimate Frisbee Club at UCI
description: We are Men's Ultimate Frisbee Club at UCI. We are a competitive club sport and regularly play other schools from California, Nevada, Utah, and Arizona. Irvine Nightlife is a competitive Ultimate Frisbee club looking for new men to join the team. We practice 2 or 3 days a week and travel to tournaments all over California and surrounding states.

The Merage Business Analytics Club is a student-run organization that aims to help members with networking opportunities, organize small workshops, engage with industry speakers and be a resource for members in the field of analytics and data science.

BTA is the bridge to the tech industry for graduate students here at Paul Merage School of Business. BTA connects UCI graduate students with opportunities at the forefront of the tech industry, focusing on roles that demand a strong foundation in both business principles and technology. The club strives to effectively leverage internal and external resources such as the career center and alumni, provide unique educational and networking experiences, and prepare members to be leaders in their post-MBA careers.

Merage C4C is a student led 501 (3)(C) non-profit organization for Merage School of Business graduate students . C4C hosts various athletic and social events to raise money for Special Olympics. We also volunteer time to Junior Achievement and Second Harvest Food Bank of Orange County. All proceeds go to these three charities.

The Merage Consulting Association at the University of California, Irvine (UCI) seeks to help students interested in the consulting profession to improve their critical thinking skills using strategic frameworks and creatively solve complex problems in quick fashion. We are devoted to building relationships between graduate students and professionals within the business consulting world. We achieve this by providing opportunities for students to learn about the accounting consulting profession as well as facilitate recruiting connections, individual growth and knowledge required for success as future business leaders.

The Merage Entertainment Management Association (EMA) is a student driven organization at The Paul Merage School of Business geared towards MBA candidates interested in careers within the entertainment media industry from sports and video games to music, film, and television. Our club facilitates networking and information sessions to better educate Merage students about the industry from a management perspective, all while introducing new and exciting career opportunities.
The Merage Financial Management Association @ UCI connects finance students and enthusiasts acrossacademic programs, bridging the gap between MFIN, FTMBA, FEMBA,EMBA, and Undergrads.
Mission to facilitate a golf community at Merage and provide a friendly environment for those who want to learn more about the game of golf.

To empower and prepare the next generation of healthcare leaders and professionals through education, networking, and community engagement. Our mission is to foster a dynamic learning environment that equips students with the knowledge, skills, and ethical values needed to excel in the ever-evolving healthcare and life sciences industries while also promoting collaboration, innovation, and a commitment to improving healthcare access and outcomes within our community.The Merage Healthcare Association offers excellent opportunities for students to learn about management careers in healthcare and the life sciences. By attending the association's networking events, students can connect with Merage alumni working in leadership positions across various healthcare organizations. These events allow students to ask questions about the day-to-day responsibilities of management roles as well as the career paths these professionals took to reach their current positions.Additionally, the Merage Healthcare Association provides students access to relevant industry events where they can gain exposure to the latest healthcare trends and innovations. Attending these events is an excellent way for students to understand the strategic challenges facing healthcare managers and the skills needed to succeed in these roles.We would encourage students interested in healthcare management to get involved with the Merage Healthcare Association. The connections and insights students can gain through this organization are invaluable in learning about the diverse management career options in the healthcare and life sciences industries. Taking advantage of these opportunities will position students for future leadership roles in these rapidly growing sectors.

About Us: What is the MMA? The Merage Marketing Association is committed to: The professional development of students interested in marketing careers. Increased corporate community awareness of the quality of Merage students. Promotion and development of Merage as an incubator of marketing and strategy talent. Strengthening relationships with alumni in various fields of marketing. MMA Events are designed to expose members to the myriad of marketing and strategy opportunities available, as well as provide a forum for strong relationship building both within Merage as well as the outside business community.

club_name: Merage Real Estate Association at UCI - MREA
description: The Merage Real Estate Association (MREA) is an active, student-run organization that complements the real estate MBA program and the Center for Real Estate at The Paul Merage School of Business. MREA adds value for its student members by offering a variety of educational events and networking opportunities where students learn from and interact with local real estate professionals and alumni. Additionally, MREA is focused on creating career-oriented opportunities for students who seek careers in the real estate industry.

The Merage Undergraduate Student Association (MUSA) is an independent student organization that collaborates with the Paul Merage School of Business to enhance the student experience. Our main goal is to promote close relationships between the students, staff, and faculty within the Merage school. MUSA also strives to enhance student's academic and professional skills by constructing and facilitating activities that maintains a strong sense of community. Lastly, MUSA serves as a link to represent the interests of the undergraduate students in order to aid their professional development as they integrate the various fields of business into their professional and educational endeavors at the University of California, Irvine.

The Merage Veterans Association at the University of California, Irvine was founded with the intention of helping military veterans from any branch of service and any ally nation as they navigate the MBA timeline. The MVA actively participates in the Orange County community by hosting special events and fundraisers for both military-focused and non-military charities.

The Women in Business club will promote awareness of issues that arise for women in business and foster support, connection, and advocacy in our community of future leaders through the provision of networking, professional, and personal development opportunities.

Our mission at Metro Theatre Company is to provide creative outlets for all undergraduate students interested in theatre and the arts, whether they are an Arts major or not. These outlets are both on stage and behind the curtain as we aim to have everyone majorly involved to be an undergraduate student.

club_name: Middle Eastern and South Asian Law Student Association
description: The purpose of this organization is to create an affinity group for UCI Law students who identify as Middle Eastern or South Asian and their allies. Specifically, programming would center around the different experiences those students face throughout law school and the legal profession generally. It will also serve as a networking and relationship building opportunity for students who share similar experiences due to their identity.

The Middle Eastern Medical Honors Association is dedicated to supporting students on their journey toward a career in medicine. While we focus on empowering students of Middle Eastern descent, our organization warmly welcomes all individuals who share our passion for medicine and community. At UCI, we strive to ease the challenges of a competitive academic environment by fostering a sense of belonging, creating a supportive network of peers, and a family-like atmosphere where students can grow, relax, and thrive together.

The Migraine Club at UCI is dedicated to raising awareness and promoting advocacy for migraine disease by providing educational resources to the campus community. In addition, the club aims to conduct research and support migraine foundations through fundraising efforts.

club_name: Military Connected Community (formerly Anteater Veteran Association)
description: The Military Connected Community is committed to providing support to our Veterans, dependents, reservists, and otherwise military-connected students. We are continuously looking for activities that will positively affect our organization, and allow our members to be actively involved. These activities include: regular club meetings used as a forum to provide participants with information, resources, and a social outlet; volunteerism with local community groups to provide service that advances the welfare of our university and greater community; and fundraising events to raise money for projects, charity, and organization enhancement.

We are an organization that promotes speed thinking and collaboration by solving different puzzles and scavenger hunt activities, as well as connecting students to local opportunities and competitions to strengthen networking within the community. We encourage diversified minds and collaboration between students and stimulate their potential.

club_name: Mock Trial Support and Hosting Association at UCI
description: MTSHA at UCI is a student-led organization dedicated to fostering leadership, event coordination, professional development, and civic engagement through the planning and hosting of intercollegiate mock trial tournaments at UC Irvine. Independently managed by UCI students, MTSHA provides opportunities for members to develop skills in tournament administration, logistics, communication, and campus programming while enriching the UCI community by bringing together students, universities, judges, attorneys, and educators through academic competition.

We exist to to Learn, Educate, Debate, and Explore the principles of the United Nations in a college environment. Our organization simulates the United Nations by recreating UN committees under which students can debate critical world issues to better understand international policies and foreign affairs. In order to achieve this educational goal we hold college and high school conferences and send our travel team around the world to competitive conferences.
Modern Completely Insane Anteaters, MCIA, is an exhibition dance team that gives its members opportunities to dance, grow, and have fun while upholding the values of respect, family, and its roots.

Mood Psychology at UCI established in 2019. We dedicate to provide high-quality psychological services for international students, including linking professional psychological counseling resources, holding academic seminars, reaching out with professors, and publishing health-related articles on the social media platform. Since UC Irvine is a diverse environment, we want to create more convenient access for international students who may experience stress from academic, life, new environment. We hope to promote the importance of psychological healthiness and help international students to relieve their stress.

The primary purpose of the Morning Sign Out (MSO) campus organization is to promote health and science literacy within the community and encourage positive and thoughtful discussions about the health and science community amongst the public via our online articles and workshops hosted. MSO at UCI aims to contribute to the greater cross-collegiate MSO parent organization.
Morse Coda A Cappella is an all-inclusive acappella group. We aim to foster a diverse and collaborative community where members can thrive and prosper musically.

Movement Exchange at University of California, Irvine is a community of globally minded individuals who share a passion for arts, education, and service to their community. Movement Exchange at University of California, Irvine will work in a domestic setting and travel abroad to empower under-resourced youth and communities through the medium of dance.

club_name: Movimiento Estudiantil Chicanx de Aztlan - MEChA
description: M.E.Ch.A is a political, educational, and cultural organization that focuses on fostering awareness of social justice issues affecting disenfranchised, underserved, and underrepresented communities; particularly the Latinx community. The organization creates various outlets and opportunities for development of educational, cultural, political, and social tools within peers and community, which is essential to fulfill our goals. M.E.Ch.A strives to provide a platform for critical consciousness that focuses on local to global community issues.

The Multicultural Sorority and Fraternity Council (MSFC) is the governing body for 18 different cultural fraternities and sororities at UC Irvine. The MSFC oversees educational programming and the promotion of the various multicultural fraternity and sorority community at UC Irvine. Groups within the MSFC have ties to Latinx, Asian, Armenian and other various multicultural backgrounds and even ties to the National Pan-Hellenic Council (NPHC).

MUSE is a student-run magazine at UCI dedicated to amplifying women’s voices at the intersection of business, fashion, and lifestyle. Our mission is to inspire and empower students by showcasing stories of leadership, creativity, and identity, while providing a platform for professional development and self-expression. In the short term, MUSE seeks to publish thought-provoking content and host engaging events that highlight student talent and foster community. In the long term, we aim to establish MUSE as a sustainable, influential publication that bridges style with strategy, empowering students to define success on their own terms and carry these values beyond campus.
Our mission is to provide a space where improv and music enthusiasts can learn to fuse the two together and improvise songs and musicals.
Our mission is to drive access to music education and performance opportunities for all, using our club as a space to destress, relax, and share music with others to heal where medicine cannot.
MLSA will create a safe space and community, advocate for the interests of Muslim law students, and cultivate connections and networks with Muslim attorneys.

The Muslim Student Union (MSU) at UC Irvine is a religious student organization which seeks to serve the Muslim student community by providing religious services and fostering social, spiritual, educational, and moral development in a way that compels Muslim students to contribute positively and uniquely to the campus community and beyond.

MTC at UCI builds a welcoming community at the intersection of Islam and technology, supporting Muslim and allied students in computer science, data science, engineering, product, and entrepreneurship through skill development, mentorship, spiritual well-being, and service.

Mycology Club at UCI gives students the opportunity to understand and appreciate anoften forgotten kingdom of life; Fungi. We explore the cultural, ecological, and clinical aspects ofmycology with engaging presentations and outings for our members. Mushrooms have been ofhigh importance historically in many cultures all over the world. They are not often seen, butthey are incredibly abundant and play an important role in our forests. There are mushroomsthat can break down plastics, and many form symbiotic relationships with trees that promote athriving ecosystem. Fungi has been used to synthesize revolutionary pharmaceuticals, such aspenicillin. A wider understanding of fungi can fight the climate crisis and save lives. Through ourorganization, our members are exposed to research, activism, hobby, and career opportunitiesthey may not have known existed. We take our members on hikes to get hands-on experiencewith locating and identifying wild species. We also allow opportunities to attend larger eventswith professional speakers, like local mushroom fairs. With great results so far, we hope toencourage more students to spend time exploring the diverse world of mycology.

club_name: Na `Opio O Ka `Aina - Hawai'i Club at UCI
description: Na `Opio O Ka `Aina exists to ease the transition of students from Hawai'i and with the goal of spreading the Aloha spirit. Na `Opio o Ka `Aina (NOOK), which translates to "The Youth of the Land", was started in 1985 by several students from Hawai'i. The original purpose of NOOK was to ease the transition of Hawai'i students to the mainland lifestyle, as well as college life. Since these students are so far away from a culture so different from the one found in Irvine, it is often difficult for them to adjust to life on the mainland. Members share the Aloha spirit and spread customs from Hawai'i to the surrounding UCI community via cultural workshops, performances, and social events. As a club, we aim to create a community that allows students from Hawai'i to feel at home on the mainland while sharing the Aloha spirit and culture from Hawai'i with as many people as possible.

National Disabled Law Student Association (NDLSA) at UCI Law aims to eliminate the stigma of disability within the legal profession, provide support for law students and prospective law students, and foster an inclusive and accessible environment for law students.NDLSA at UCI Law asserts that the ideal way to make UCI Law accessible for students is to enact widespread non-exclusionary change that benefits the entire community. However, NDLSA at UCI Law acknowledges that in cases where this is not possible, it is still important to advocate for each student getting their needs met in an individualized manner.

club_name: National Lawyers Guild at UCI - NLG
description: The University of California, Irvine, School of Law ("UCI Law") Chapter of the National Lawyers Guild ("NLG") is an association dedicated to the support and defense of economic and social justice, and to progressive change rather than the acceptance of the status quo. We seek to educate ourselves and the community about issues affecting economic and social justice, to provide law students with pro bono opportunities in support of these goals, and to increase awareness of the UCI community on issues surrounding economic and social justice. We seek to unite the lawyers, law students, legal workers and jailhouse lawyers of America in an organization which shall function as an effective political and social force in the service of the people, to the end that economic and social justice are basic human rights and must be protected and expanded.
Our mission is to increase the number of culturally responsible Black engineers who excel academically succeed professionally and positively impact the community.

club_name: National Society of Leadership and Success [The]
description: The National Society of Leadership and Success is an organization that assists people in discovering and achieving their goals. Members will learn how to achieve their goals through the Society's leadership speaker series as well as through being part of a community where like minded success-oriented individuals come together and help one another. In addition, not only will the members succeed in their own lives, but they will also create a better world through community service and cooperation. The core philosophy of the society is for our members to achieve their dreams with meaningful support and dedicated action.

club_name: National Student Speech Language Hearing Association Chapter at UCI - NSSLHA
description: Our mission is to bridge the gap created by the absence of a dedicated Communication Science and Disorders (CSD) program at UCI, fostering professional interest and providing essential resources to students pursuing research or clinical careers in Speech-Language Pathology and Audiology.

The mission of the Native American Law Students Association is to gather Indigenous students and allies to create community; discuss Indigenous socio-legal issues and ongoing affairs; emphasize the study of tribal and federal Indian law and the effect of law on Indigenous communities; promote Indigenous wellness; recruit Indigenous students and faculty; and provide volunteer and service opportunities in support of Indigenous communities.Indigenous refers to any of the original peoples of North America, South America, and Oceania. We emphatically disavow the use of blood quantum, which is a tool of genocide, as a measure of indigeneity, instead emphasizing community, family, and tribal affiliation, and values. NALSA is open to Indigenous students and allies.NALSA is a pending chapter of the National Native American Law Students Association.
To advance the gospel of Jesus and His kingdom into the nations through spiritual generations of laborers living and discipling among the lost.

The Neonatal Nursing Club (NNC) is a student-led organization dedicated to advancing education, advocacy, and professional development in neonatal nursing. The club provides opportunities for UCI health students to gain hands-on experience, mentorship, and networking with healthcare professionals, particularly in the Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU).The organization emphasizes evidence-based practice, family-centered care, and the integration of classroom knowledge with real-world clinical experiences.
