NNC aims to empower and support health students to excel academically, achieve their health-related educational goals, and prepare for successful careers in neonatal and pediatric nursing.By creating a safe, inclusive space for collaboration, discussion, and skill development, the club fosters leadership, career readiness, and lifelong learning. Through events, workshops, and community engagement, NNC also raises awareness about ongoing challenges in maternal and infant health, including disparities that impact diverse populations. The club seeks to inspire the next generation of neonatal nurses to deliver high-quality, compassionate care, while providing opportunities for personal growth, professional networking, and academic excellence.

New Forum is a publication dedicated to UC Irvine's undergraduate creative writing. We take submissions of short fiction, poetry, and original artwork every quarter, and selected submissions will be printed in our quarterly publication. At New Forum, we look for compelling storytelling and language that unzips and makes us see again.
We are a Christian organization serving Chinese-speaking students enrolled at UC Irvine. We aim to help students know Jesus Christ and His Gospel.

The Nigerian Student Association at the University of California, Irvine is firmly committed to uniting and strengthening the Nigerian and greater African community at UCI for the purposes of networking, cultural enrichment, open dialogue, and civic engagement.

The Nihon Karate Club at UCI is a beginner-friendly club that pursues both the recreational and competitive aspects of the Japanese martial art of Karate. We strive for mental and physical self-improvement as we develop self-defense skills, continue Japanese Karate culture traditions, and cultivate a strong Karate community. We are also a competitive sports club associated with the World Karate Federation and Japanese Karate-Do Jinen Kai.Whether you have some experience or none at all, we welcome you to join our club! Please don't hesitate to reach out if you have questions.

club_name: No Voice Alone Acapella - NOVA Acapella
description: NOVA is a diverse, all-gender a cappella group at the University of California, Irvine. We are dedicated to helping each member grow as a vocalist and performer through guidance, collaboration, and creativity.

club_name: NORD Students for Rare Chapter at UC Irvine
description: The mission of NORD Students for Rare Chapters is to increase awareness about treatments and care for patients with rare and chronic disorders. Further we aim to allow students the opportunity to network with professionals in the field rare disease research and care to push the boundaries of knowledge in the field of rare disorders while we provide them with more knowledge about how to pursuit a career in healthcare and its requirements.

Nu Alpha Kappa Fraternity, Inc. Psi Chapter at UC Irvine was established on August 18, 2012. We're a Latino-based fraternity that encompasses and values all cultures. We pride ourselves in our three pillars of Academic Excellence, Culture, Brotherhood. Through these pillars, we pride ourselves in being "Men of Mind...Men of Culture...Men of Pride." It is also through these pillars that we aim to improve our campus and surrounding communities with events that will empower our academic endeavors as well as inspiring gentlemen from all backgrounds to seek leadership, community service, and academic-success.

Nu Rho Psi at UCI is a chapter of the Nu Rho Psi National Honor Society. Our mission is to develop the next generation of neuroscientists and shape their career trajectories by providing immersive research, training, community outreach, and professional development experiences.

The Nuestra Grad committee is in charge of the annual NUESTRA GRADUATION. This is an annual event for Chicana/o Latinx students who wish to participate in a more intimate celebration in addition to the regular UCI commencement ceremonies. The event is a bilingual and bi-cultural celebration that is open to all students and UCI community that honors Latinx students personal success and academic achievement in higher education. The program allows graduates to recognize their family, friends, and others who have provided support and encouragement during their college years.

club_name: Nursing Science Student Association at UCI
description: Our mission is to provide resources, opportunities, and a network that enhances the educational experience and professional development of our members.

The primary purpose of the Ocean Club is to foster a community of individuals who share a passion for exploring and learning about the ocean and its surrounding environments, such as beaches, tide pools, and marine ecosystems. This club serves as a platform for students to connect, engage in ocean-related activities, and promote marine conservation awareness.

The purpose of this organization is to foster a supportive and thriving community for students who have taken time off prior to law school, are transitioning into second careers, have previously pursued an advanced degree, have families, are parents, and others who view their academic path as non-traditional.

Open Jam is a community that aims to create music performance, collaboration, and appreciation opportunities for students at UCI. We not only foster a community within our club, but contribute to the schoolwide community through coordinating events and performances with other groups. We welcome members of any and all skill levels, and encourage the development of musical skills through events such as open mic nights and group lessons-- All that is required to join Open Jam is a desire to appreciate and play music! Check our Facebook page for more information and time and meeting locations, or our Instagram or Youtube channel to see videos of club members' performances.

The mission of “OCC@UCI” is to cultivate interest in optical and photonic computing and to developan interdisciplinary community at UCI centered on light-based information processing.The club is dedicated to provide a platform for engagement in discussion and empoweringstudents with the skills to design, simulate, and implement computational systems that leverageoptics. By centering the club around a Journal Club, members will critically discuss and analyzescholarly work related to optical computing architectures and photonic information systems. Tosupplement these discussions, the club hosts educational seminars introducing foundational andadvanced concepts from optics, machine learning, and engineering, as well as project-based workshops designed to reinforce and apply the material covered.

club_name: Orange County Chapter of the Association of Environmental Professionals at UCI (OCAEP)
description: The Association of Environmental Professionals (AEP) is a non-profit organization established to facilitate greater relationships between professionals and students interested in environmental related jobs and to foster the mutual professional growth of our members through those relationships.

Order of Omega is a leadership honor society for members of Greek organizations. Order of Omega recognizes juniors and seniors who have exemplified high standards in the areas of scholarship, leadership, involvement within their respective organization and within the Greek, campus, and local community. Members are selected from the top 3% of students at each institution. To date, over 500 chapters have been chartered throughout North America, each sharing the common goal of recognizing the many outstanding student leaders at their institution.

club_name: Ordinary College South Orange County at UCI
description: The mission of Ordinary College South Orange County is to help students find a community that will prioritize their spiritual lives and the kingdom of God by studying the Gospel and spending time to fellowship with one another.
OCF transforms the lives of college students by guiding them along the path to Jesus Christ through His Church, cultivating a campus community of worship, witness, service, fellowship, and education.
osu! at UCI is a community made for individuals interested in osu!, a free, multiplayer rhythm game.

OutLaw at UCI Law facilitates civic and social activities by and for the lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender, queer, intersex, and asexual (LGBTQIA+) community at UCI Law through education, community empowerment, and activism. Education and Scholarship: OutLaw at UCI Law promotes discussions about the intersections of sexual orientation, gender identity, race, ethnicity, and the law. LGBTQIA+ communities experience unique challenges to attaining access to justice and inclusion in the legal industry. Many LGBTQIA+ clients lack access to competent representation. They face unfriendly legal precedent, attacks from legislatures, and disparate enforcement. We seek to highlight local and national conversations about these issues and to provide opportunities for related scholarship at UCI Law. Recently, OutLaw was awarded funding for a multi-day symposium on legal issues that affect transgender communities. Community Empowerment: OutLaw provides networking, social, and leadership opportunities for LGBTQIA+ students, faculty, staff, and alumni. We support and empower each other to become stronger advocates and legal professionals by holding space for LGBTQIA+ members of the UCI Law community. Please contact receive updates about upcoming events. Activism: OutLaw connects UCI Law community members with opportunities to advocate for the safety, inclusion, and equality of people of all sexual orientations and gender identities. We encourage all OutLaw members to participate in pro bono projects that serve local LGBTQIA+ communities, such as the Transgender Legal Assistance Clinic at the LGBT Center OC in Santa Ana. Become a Member: All currently enrolled J.D. and LLM students at UCI Law are eligible to be members, including joint degree program participants, faculty, and staff.

The Pakistani Student Association is an on-campus cultural club dedicated to expressing our heritage, educating Pakistanis and Non-Pakistanis alike, and creating a social atmosphere to make lifelong friends in. With the help of our Board and club members, we have a history of throwing spectacular culture shows, successful fundraisers, and have shown just how rich our culture truly is. This year we strive to take that one step further and keep our community involved as much as possible, because in the end, we must keep our culture alive.

The Panhellenic Association serves as the collegiate governing body of the 7 National Panhellenic Conference sororities on the UC Irvine campus. The Panhellenic Council is composed of 12 executive board officers. The Panhellenic Association works to unite sorority women on common goals, create a network of support for chapters and members, and serve our SFL and University community. We sponsor interactive programs and activities not only for sorority women, but for all students, such as educational speakers, scholarship programs, and quarterly Risk Events.

To establish a cultural initiative centered around Giddha, a traditional folk dance form originating from the Punjab region, we aim to create an inclusive platform for our community at UC Irvine. While traditionally performed by women, we welcome all interested participants to join us in celebrating this vibrant and expressive art form. Driven by the absence of a Giddha team at UC Irvine, we seek to fill this gap and provide a space for individuals from diverse backgrounds to come together and experience the joy of Giddha. This initiative is not just about preserving cultural heritage but also about fostering unity, expression, and storytelling through dance and music. Giddha offers a unique opportunity for participants to connect with their cultural roots, express emotions, and build strong bonds of friendship and camaraderie. By opening this initiative to all, we hope to promote diversity, inclusivity, and cross-cultural understanding within our campus community. Through workshops, performances, and collaborative events, we invite everyone to join us in exploring the beauty and significance of Giddha.

The purpose of Patient Navigation Network at UCI is to reduce barriers to healthcare access and improve continuity of care in partnership with local clinics, senior residences, hospices, and community organizations by providing structured, non-clinical patient navigation and practical patient education.

The Pharmaceutical Sciences Mentorship Program (PSMP) is designed to help incoming students ease the transition from high school or college to a university. This program provides students with the opportunity to be paired with a current Pharm Sci student to learn more about UCI and the Pharm Sci major. Incoming students will not only get the chance to gain deeper insight about the campus, its resources, programs, and major, but they will also create friendships with their mentor and other mentees. In addition, mentors and mentees will participate in various socials throughout the academic year in order to help build connections with peers and other Pharmaceutical Sciences programs.

The mission of PSC is to foster a community within undergraduate Pharmaceutical Science majors through student advocacy, establishing professional relationships, and providing career related opportunities for the development of our future professions as part of a greater effort to help students achieve greater academic success.

Phi Beta Delta at the University of California, Irvine is dedicated to recognizing and promoting academic excellence, leadership, and cross-cultural understanding within the Hispanic and international communities. Our mission is to empower scholars of Hispanic heritage and those committed to global engagement through scholarship, service, and cultural exchange. We strive to create a supportive community that celebrates diversity and prepares members to lead with compassion and commitment to positive change in an interconnected world. Through our collaboration with the Spanish Department and their faculty and graduate students, we aim to create opportunities for all interested in better understanding and celebrating our individuality.

To provide a forum wherein Physicians and Students of medicine may cometogether, to their mutual benefit, in a brotherhood seeking the development ofthe higher qualities of medicine; of nobler impulses of heart; of more profoundscholastic achievement; of devotion to the art and science of medicine; and of acommunion of kindred hearts pledged to support each other in times of joy, aswell as adversity.

To promote the cause of higher business education and training for all individuals, to foster high ideals for everyone pursuing a career in business; to encourage fraternity and cooperation among people preparing for such careers; and to stimulate the spirit of sacrifice and unselfish devotion to the attainment of such ends.

club_name: Phi Delta Epsilon Medical Fraternity - CA Epsilon
description: Phi Delta Epsilon International Medical Fraternity creates physicians of integrity with a lifelong commitment to our guiding principles of philanthropy, deity, and education through fellowship, service, mentoring, and formal training in leadership, science, and ethics. Our organization is the only professional fraternity on campus to provide singular, specialized help to all pre-medical students. We promote a familial environment to assist them on the rigorous path to medical school along with holding philanthropic and educational events throughout the year to showcase our excellence. We offer everyone the opportunity to be a part of the larger international organization that spans the entire nation to help build a grand network by the time they graduate and apply.

Phi Gamma Delta exists to promote lifelong friendships, to reaffirm high ethical standards and values, and to foster personal development in the pursuit of excellence. Phi Gamma Delta is committed to providing opportunities to each brother to develop responsibility, leadership, scholarship, and social skills in order to become a fully contributing member of society.

The Phi Kappa Psi Fraternity is committed to bettering individuals in order to improve society. To that end, we strive to provide undergraduate members with the opportunity to get as much out of their campus experience as possible, while working within their chapters to effect change in their communities. Over 70,000 alumni provide a foundation of support for our undergraduates and are able to band together as Phi Psis through Alumni Associations across the nation. Mission The Phi Kappa Psi Fraternity is an association of men of integrity who strive to develop the individual in his intellect, in his involvement in the community, and in his faith. Recognizing and valuing the diversity of all, the Fraternity unites the principals and traditions of our past with the resources and creativity of our present to provide an environment in which our members can realize their highest potential. To this end, we offer a lifelong experience, guided by our faith in a power greater than ourselves, in contributing to the betterment of both the individual and the community.

The purpose of Phi Lambda Rho Sorority, Inc. is to provide a lifelong sisterhood based on facilitating the advancement of women of color through higher education. Our mission is to give back to our community, especially our marginalized youth while celebrating and promoting the Chicana/Latina culture.
Photonics @ UCI is the local student chapter for the Optical Society of America (OPTICA) and Society for Optics and Photonics (SPIE).

club_name: Physician Assistants Coming Together at UCI - PACT
description: Our mission is to help educate and prepare students for the physician assistant profession. We strive to assist members in gaining more knowledge about the profession, application process, and various healthcare experiences. In addition to our networking opportunities, we host workshops, community service events, fundraisers, and socials to create a supportive environment for pre-PA students.

The Physics Grad Caucus seeks to enhance the physics graduate student experience in three primary ways: To provide a voice for physics graduate students in departmental affairs. To facilitate scientific and social interaction between physics graduate students of all different subfields. To provide physics graduate students a forum beyond official department channels to improve their education, research, and prospects for postgraduate work.
The mission of Pi Beta Phi Fraternity for women is to promote friendship, develop women of intellect and integrity, cultivate leadership potential and enrich lives through community service.
Pi Kappa Alpha is dedicated to developing men of integrity, intellect, and high moral character and to fostering a truly lifelong fraternal experience.
This organization’s mission is to create a welcoming, social environment for the UCI community to enjoy pickleball as a sport through recreational and competitive play.

Pilipinx Pre-Health Undergraduate Student Organization (PUSO) is a social and academic organization with the following goals: 1. To provide service, guidance, and support to pre-health students. 2. To sponsor programs for minority youth to encourage their entrance into health professions. 3. To increase the number of culturally sensitive health care professionals. 4. To serve the campus and the community of Irvine as well as the Pilipino community at large. 5. To spread "PUSO Love."

Pilipinx-Americans in Social Studies (PASS) is an organization that focuses on fields relating to business, law, humanities, social sciences, and social ecology. PASS is a “community within a community” striving to increase the representation of Pilipinxs/Filipinxs and other minorities within professional industries while providing a social support network that promotes academic excellence, career development, community involvement, and leadership opportunities for students in the UCI (University of California, Irvine) and Pilipinx/Filipinx communities.

Planned Parenthood Generation Action at the University of California, Irvine (hereinafter referred to as PPGA at UCI) exists to educate the university community about reproductive health and rights, to translate increased awareness into pro-choice activism on campus, and to serve as a coalition partner to state, national, and international reproductive rights efforts.PPGA at UCI believes in the fundamental right of every individual to manage their fertility. PPGA at UCI supports full access to comprehensive reproductive and complementary health care services in settings that preserve and protect the essential privacy and rights of each individual; advocates for public policies that guarantee these rights and ensure access to such services; and supports access to medically accurate educational programs that enhance understanding of human sexuality.PPGA at UCI extends its activism not only to reproductive rights but to reproductive justice, as defined by Sister Song as the human right to maintain personal bodily autonomy, have children, not have children, and parent the children we have in safe and sustainable communities.PPGA at UCI intends to destigmatize sex, sexuality, and reproductive health by increasing health literacy and awareness to the campus community about available services, resources, and general education.

Platypus at UCI serves as a campus chapter of the Platypus Affiliated Society. The Platypus Affiliated Society, established in December 2006, organizes reading groups, public fora, research and journalism focused on the problems and tasks inherited from the "Old" (1920s–30s), "New" (1960s–70s) and post-political (1980s–90s) Left for the possibilities of emancipatory politics today.

The Poker Strategy Club provides a learning environment where students can study and practice poker as a strategic game. Our mission is to teach both foundational and modern poker concepts—from game theory optimal (GTO) play and pot odds to adaptive strategies such as exploitative play—while exploring decision-making, probability, and psychology in a fun, social, and no-stakes setting.

club_name: Politics, Unity, Noize, and Knowledge club
description: The P.U.N.K Club was formed in a time where public injustice was on the rise and community service was at an all time low. Our club is made to educate and empower the youth about current situations that affect different sectors of the world to cause a positive change. We aim to encourage a new generation's leaders, uplift empathy, and increase meaningful volunteer hours.

Powerlifting Club at UCI was founded by Rainee Khabagnote and EJ Torralba in 2014. The Club has grown to become a well-known and respected Collegiate Powerlifting Team. We are both a competitive and recreational team with many members holding American and State records. Our members primarily compete in the USAPL; however, some compete in the USPA. Our focus is assisting every member in reaching their full potential as both an individual and also as part of something bigger than themselves. Important Facts: - All members must register with UCI Club Sports and pay the $15 fee - There will be optional meetings/practices TBD

club_name: Pre-Dental Society at UC Irvine - PDS
description: The Pre-Dental Society at UC Irvine is dedicated to helping students on their journey in pursuing a career in dentistry. We strive to create the best environment for pre-dental students through meetings with Dental School Representatives, workshops, field trips, presentations, community service and social events. We provide opportunities for students to gain valuable knowledge and insight into dentistry in an environment where students are able to network with one another and build friendships. Our members are given opportunities to strengthen their application for dental school through building their leadership skills in an altruistic environment.

Spreading awareness to the community as a pre-health organization working with all fields of medicine while educating our members on the available careers of healthcare to pursue. Here we aim to network amongst various influential organizations in hopes of educating and inspiring the general public and future health care professionals. We promote an interdisciplinary approach by working with all aspects of healthcare through community outreach, as well as clinical environments, while fostering network opportunities with healthcare professionals.

Our mission as the Pre-Health Club at UCI is to inspire and empower pre-health students by providing a comprehensive education, supportive mentorship, and motivational resources to guide students on their pre-health journeys. We are dedicated to fostering a collaborative environment that builds a community that fosters growth, resilience, and encouragement that leads to the success of students’ careers as pre-health students. Through engaging events, thoughtful speakers, and various health-related opportunities offered, we aim to prepare our members to become competent healthcare workers and make meaningful contributions to the health and well-being of others.

As the Pre-Law Latinx Association at the University of California, Irvine, we believe in increasing Latinx matriculation in post-grad avenues alongside law programs that serve to increase educational attainment within the Latinx community. We strive to develop a network of social support with resources easily available to students in the forms of mentorship, LSAT preparation, law school program preparedness, personal statement workshops, guest speakers involved in the legal field, and skill-development to enhance students' preparedness to succeed in law school. We hope to establish an ever-growing Latinx-based club at UCI that will strive to create a welcoming community for all marginalized students, predominantly identifying of Latinx descent, seeking to attend law school and/or pursue in the legal fields.

Pre-Law Society at UC Irvine is dedicated to assisting UC Irvine undergraduates who are looking to pursue a career in law or legal studies. Our organization strives to provide UC Irvine undergraduates with tools needed to be successful in law schools such as opportunities to see lawyers on the job, create connections, develop leadership skills and more hands-on experiences in the field of law. Pre-Law Society hosts diverse programs (e.g., LSAT informational seminars, law school admissions panel, as well as speaker panels) to help UCI undergraduates reach an informed decision about their career.

To create and support fellow UCI students who are interested in Occupational Therapy, while also providing them with the resources and opportunities they may need towards their path to becoming a successful therapist.

A campus organization based on student leadership and team building, Pre-Pharmacy Society (PPS) at UCI is dedicated to providing a social environment that encourages students interested in pharmacy to thrive as competitive applicants and as student leaders. We offer the tools necessary to approach the field with confidence through presented information (i.e. general insight, academia requirements, healthcare industry, etc.) and hands-on experience (i.e. volunteer, internship, jobs, etc.). By utilizing guest speaker, pharmacy school trips, community service events, and networking opportunities, PPS at UCI engages the aptitude of students to help them decide whether or not to pursue the field of pharmacy.

The Pre-Veterinary and Animal Wellness Association (PAWA) is dedicated to helping animals and supporting students exploring careers in animal care and veterinary medicine. Through volunteering, networking, and hands-on experiences, we introduce undergraduates to pathways in veterinary science and related fields. Our mission is to educate, empower, and connect students who share a genuine passion for animal welfare. We host guest speakers, organize field trips, and facilitate access to programs that provide direct animal care experience, while fostering a strong sense of community through social events and peer support.

PRISM Outreach serves to foster a positive, inclusive, and intersectional community for queer students of all identities, providing both social and material support in the campus community. PRISM strives to create a safe space for every individual to explore their identity and learn from the experiences of others.

The purpose of the Prison Education Project at UCI is to educate, engage, and empower the communities affected by the American Legal System and UC Irvine students to bring this social justice issue at the forefront of student conversations. As a club, we have three core values: education, social justice, and political advocacy. These values are interconnected and are a guide for our club projects, fundraising efforts, and educational material to ensure we address the United States' social and political aspects of the carceral system.

Our mission at Pro-Health Journal Club is to create a new community that serves as a platform for engaging students in different fields of STEM/Social Sciences through their mutual interest in healthcare. This will be accomplished through guiding students in their efforts to comprehend and discuss scientific journals through academic discourse, collaboration and presentations. Students will develop scientific literacy and communication skills necessary to succeed in professional/graduate schools. Strong knowledge in advanced health-related topics will be learnt and help prepare students for upper division courses and potential research labs. All UCI students who are majoring in or are simply interested in learning about at least one of the 8 different areas of healthcare are encouraged to join this community. Pro-Health Journal Club (PHC) will demonstrate the Interconnectedness of the different healthcare fields and guide its students to become informed and educated members of society who seek evidence-based knowledge.
To foster a community of students interested in product management and related disciplines while enabling them with resources for early-career readiness.

Our mission is to promote innovation, creativity and develop a student community of forwardthinkers, builders, and product leaders at UCI by focusing on practical learning.We are a student organization initiated by MBA students at the Paul Merage School of Businessat UCI. We got together to create a community of product leaders, bridge knowledge gaps,cultivate innovation, and help each other to launch a successful professional career.Our club facilitates networking and information sessions to better educate Merage studentsabout product management, all while introducing new and exciting career opportunities.

We aim to serve impoverished areas and families by providing entirely free tennis clinics, introducing children to the benefits of fitness and hobbies while tutoring and instructing them. Through mentorship and accessible athletic education, we hope to empower youth with confidence, discipline, and a lifelong appreciation for healthy recreation and community engagement.

Established in 2016, Project Renegade is a project team based at the University of California, Irvine(UCI). Composed of dancers from across the Irvine Dance Community, our mission exceedsartistic endeavors; we aspire to provide a community for dancers to immerse themselves in theart form and embrace the joy derived from dance. As a testament to our ethos, we aim to focuson the enjoyable aspects of dance: creating a space where our members can have fun andusing dance as an outlet from the stressful nature of competitive dance. Project Renegade iscommitted to upholding the essence of passion and creativity with a lively atmosphere thatfosters a sense of enjoyment for all dancers involved.

club_name: Project RISHI (Rural India Social and Health Improvement) at UCI
description: Project Rishi at UCI is meant to focus on the social and health improvement of rural areas in India. It is a non-profit student-led organization dedicated to promoting the sustainable development and growth of these international communities. Our mission is to advance various aspects of life quality by collaborating with local NGOs, NPOs, and community partners. Through active student involvement, we aim to combine research, innovation, and service to create meaningful change. Our members will work by organizing awareness campaigns, fundraisers, and mission trips to rural villages in India, where prepared committees focus on key areas such as clinical health, reproductive health, environmental sustainability, and computer literacy. Together we strive to create long-term, community-driven solutions that improve access to healthcare, promote education, and empower individuals through knowledge and opportunity.We also hope to encourage and promote empathy for cultural awareness and sensitivity for all UCI students, regardless of ethnicity and cultural heritage. It is an opportunity for engagement with multiple cultures, where the Asian American perspective connects to a global initiative.

Project Shifa at UCI empowers immigrants, refugees, and marginalized students by expanding access to education, mentorship, wellness resources, and culturally responsive support. We work to bridge gaps in opportunity through community-centered programs that prioritize dignity, representation, and long-term growth.

The purpose of this organization is dedicated to supporting educationally and economically disadvantaged Vietnamese individuals in the Orange County area. We strive to provide unique resources and assistance including COVID-19 vaccines, mental health aid and awareness, etc. Additionally, Project Vietnam encourages medical missions to Vietnam, focusing on delivering primary, surgical, and pediatric emergency care services to those who lack access due to financial or medical barriers.

Psychology Student Association is an academic and social club for Psychology majors and other students interested in the field. Our mission is to offer valuable information to members in an effort to enrich each one with the knowledge and confidence to pursue a graduate education, and eventually a career in Psychology. Whether it be campus resources, internships, volunteer and research opportunities, preparedness for graduate school, a space to meet fellow students interested in the field of psychology, pursue a passion, or information about careers in Psychology and related fields, PSA strives to keep its members well informed and connected to networks of other students and faculty. We provide our members with leadership, and community service opportunities, and encourage them to become active members of the UCI community.
The purpose of PHMP is to build community among the Public Health undergraduates by connecting new students with continuing students to develop long-term mentor-mentee relationships.

club_name: Public Policy Student Association at UCI - PPSA
description: The Public Policy Student Association (PPSA) seeks to empower and equip students of UC Irvine to become the next generation of public policy experts.

Punjabis at UC Irvine (PAI) exists to celebrate and promote the rich heritage of Punjabi culture. Our purpose is to create a vibrant community for individuals who share a passion for Punjabi traditions, language, and values. Through a variety of events, educational programs, and cultural activities, we aim to raise awareness and foster appreciation for Punjabi culture within our community and beyond.

club_name: Pyo Alliance of Community Health and Education at UCI
description: Our mission is to unite premed students with a passion for community service, fostering a commitment to healthcare, volunteerism, and professional growth. Through hands-on service projects, volunteering, & public health initiatives, we strive to make a meaningful impact on underserved communities while preparing our members for careers in medicine. By combining education, outreach, and collaboration, we aim to make ourselves into compassionate future healthcare professionals dedicated to service and advocacy.

QT STEM is an organization at UCI for queer and/or trans people who are part of the STEM fields. With this group, we hope to create a more visible LGBTQ+ community in what can be an underrepresented area of academia. We also encourage allies to join! However, LGBTQ+ voices and experiences will be centered. As a campus organization, we work to build support systems and connections to resources for LGBTQ+ people at the all levels of the campus community (undergraduate, graduate, postdoctoral, technicians, staff, faculty) in STEM fields. We organize weekly meetings to share and discuss topics related to the intersection of our identities and our areas of study. We also seek involvement from LGBTQ+ members of the professional community who would like to share their stories with us.

At the Quantum Computing Club, we’re all about unlocking the power of quantum software and building a vibrant quantum community at UCI! Whether you're a total beginner or already dreaming in qubits, we’re here to help you design, experiment, and innovate with real quantum algorithms. But we don’t stop there! We love crossing boundaries—from machine learning to optimization and beyond—exploring how quantum computing can revolutionize different fields. With hands-on projects, collabs, and a passion for the future, we’re shaping the next wave of quantum pioneers.For more information, check out our website: https://www.qc-uci.club

Queer & Asian at UCI (Q&A) is an organization focused on the intersections of LGBTQ+, Asian, and Pacific Islander (API) identities. This group exists to engender a space, where Q&A identified individuals can share resources, find community, and peer support.

Foster academic, professional, and personal growth through mentorship, networking, and skill-building opportunities.Promote cultural pride and representation within the dental field.Educate members about dental school preparation, community service, and oral health awareness.Collaborate with local dental professionals and organizations to provide outreach and volunteering opportunities.

Rang De Irvine is the only Bhangra team at UCI. Bhangra is a dance that originated in Punjabi known for its very high energy and colorful performances. Our team has been around for 3 years and we have performed at competitions as far as Davis, CA and are previous reigning champions of Soulstice (UCI's annual talent show). We are open to a variety of experience levels; even if you have never tried bhangra before come join us at one of the future workshops! We are so excited to meet all of you and have you be a part of our bhangra family!

REACH at UCI's mission is to empower aspiring creators, marketers, and social media enthusiasts by connecting them with professional opportunities, and providing a space for those interested in the social media or marketing field to collaborate with one another and grow professionally.

The mission of this initiative is to strengthen existing partnerships, in addition to fostering new collaborations, between high school science programs and UCI research labs. Additionally, we seek to help graduate students sharpen their science communication and teaching skills. Altogether, we hope to inspire young students to pursue careers in science, and ultimately, help to increase their preparedness for college-level study. Our vision is that these efforts will lead to the University and the scientific enterprise overall becoming more accessible to the community at large.

club_name: Real Estate Association at UCI- REA
description: Real Estate Association is an undergraduate student organization with the purpose of bringing together a community of students at UCI that is interested in the field of real estate. Open to all majors and backgrounds, our club provides opportunities for undergraduates to learn more about real estate, develop their leadership and professional skills, and to further their passion for service to the community. We also promote student awareness of the potential career opportunities in the field of real estate by connecting our members to professionals in different aspects of the real estate industry through a wide variety of speakers and events. REA serves to educate and connect students of UC Irvine about the Real Estate Industry and its different career and investment opportunities. Our partnership with the Center For Real Estate at UCI provides us with job/scholarship opportunities and many educational resources to provide to our members. Through our association, students have the opportunity to find successful mentors with established careers in the industry, connect with other students interested in Real Estate, learn leadership/professional skills, and further their passion for service in the community.
RUF is a Christian ministry for UCI students to come and explore together who Jesus is. We want his life, death, and resurrection to shape our friendships, our thinking, and our campus.

club_name: Reframing Civil and Environmental Engineering at UCI - CEER
description: CEER is a coalition of undergraduate students, graduate students and postdocs from UCI CEE working to promote Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion (DEI) both within our department and the university as a whole. We formed this group because we sensed a gap in the discussion and education of social, environmental, political, and economic issues within the department's curriculum, and desire to ensure that the department's Anti-Racism Task Force is making progress toward shaping a school where students feel fully represented. We are committed to working with CEE Department leadership to achieve our goals. We strongly believe that moving towards racial justice and social equity is the responsibility of every civil and environmental engineer.

Regents Scholar Society at UCI is dedicated to cultivating a community of scholars who embody academic excellence, meaningful service, and transformative leadership. Through mentorship, academic resources, and leadership opportunities, we empower our members to grow, succeed, and thrive — on campus and beyond UCI — while making a lasting impact in their communities. We also strive to create a healthy, and welcoming environment for all members, and for those who are just coming into UCI.

The mission of the Repair Cafe at UCI is to provide UCI students with the opportunity to utilize their technical skills to help the local community repair their broken items, with the ultimate goal of reducing waste and promoting sustainable consumption in Orange County. This includes electronics, clothing, bicycles, furniture, and much more. UCI students will also have the opportunity to learn new skills from other volunteers through technical workshops, who bring their own diverse talents and experiences to the Repair Cafe.

We are a 100% student-led, peer-support organization focused on connecting undergraduate students to research opportunities at UCI. By connecting skateboarders at UCI, the club focuses on further Members' skateboarding skills and interests. club_name: Society for Advancement of Chicanos/Hispanics and Native Americans in Science (SACNAS)

club_name: Society of Engineers, Scientists, and Entrepreneurs at UCI
description: The Society of Engineers, Scientists, and Entrepreneurs (SESE) at UCI hosts career fairs and research seminars to empower student engineers, scientists, and entrepreneurs by fostering meaningful connections with industry leaders and academic pioneers. SESE facilitates dialogue between Berkeley’s top engineering talent and influential figures, including Nobel laureates, bridging academia and industry. By consistently delivering exceptional talent to both sectors, SESE plays a vital role in providing resources, career opportunities, and academic pathways, fulfilling its mission to advance the future of engineering and innovation.

club_name: Society of Graduate Electrical Engineers and Computer Scientists at University of California, Irvine

Our mission is to be an organization that can help undergraduate physics students academically and to provide a hub where undergraduates of any year can interact with one another.

The Society of Women Engineers (SWE) is a chapter of a national not-for-profit educational and service organization that empowers women to succeed and advance in the field of engineering, and to be recognized for their life-changing contributions as engineers and leaders. Founded in 1950, SWE is the driving force that establishes engineering as a highly desirable career for women through an exciting array of training and development programs, networking opportunities, scholarships, outreach and advocacy activities. Our mission, adopted in 1986, is to 1) stimulate and support women of all ages to achieve full potential in careers as engineers and leaders, 2) expand the image of the engineering profession as an innovative and driving force in improving the quality of life, and 3) demonstrate the value of diversity. SWE’s objectives, adopted in 1950, are to 1) Inform young women, their parents, counselors, and the general public, of the qualifications and achievements of women engineers and the opportunities open to them, 2) assist women in readying themselves for a return to active work after temporary retirement, 3) serve as a center of information on women in engineering, and 4) encourage women engineers to attain high levels of education and professional achievement.

Soon Movement is dedicated to creating movements on campuses through believers who are committed to connecting people to Christ. club_name: Southern California Health Outreach at UCI
description: At SCHO, we believe health insurance information should be understandable and readily accessible to all. By providing free-of-cost educational materials and informational sessions to underinsured populations, we aim to demystify the enrollment process, help individuals and families navigate the healthcare system, and expand coverage in Los Angeles and beyond.This group is designed to expand access to healthcare primarily under the ACA, but also under Medicare, Medicaid, etc. We will go into the community and assist underserved populations by directly assisting them with signing up for a plan, and keeping in touch with them to ensure no gaps in coverage. We will partner with other community organizations, and student groups on campus to set up educational events and fairs in the community related to healthcare eligibility and enrollment-- and at these events, we will also attempt to insure as many people as possible. In the future, we will design our own procedure for signing up uninsured individuals and compare the efficacy of this process with the standard protocol. We are not doing political advocacy, or health/wellness fairs—we are simply helping people who normally would not access insurance, get coverage.

The UCl Space Law Society examines the current laws governing human activity in space and possible future developments. The UCI Space Law Society seeks to familiarize students with this body of law through courses, events, and partnerships with outside organizations.

Foster academic and intellectual debate with students within UCI and amongst the UC's, collaborating with debate clubs of other universities to host tournaments and meets. The Sports Medicine Club at UCI (SMED) educates about sports medicine and its associated skills and professions by providing interactive workshops, guest speakers, on- and off-campus volunteering opportunities, and an introduction to the UCI Sports Performance Internship. SMED acts as a nexus between learning and socializing with its emphasis on establishing a UCI community bonded by a willingness to help others and passion for athletics. All activities organized by SMED will abide by this purpose.

Sprout Up provides free, youth-led environmental education programs to Kindergarten, 1st and 2nd grade classrooms in public schools located in the Irvine area. Our college student-instructors teach children vital concepts in environmental science and sustainability during the earliest stages of their educational development, cultivating the next generation of passionate caretakers of the earth. Through activities, experiments, and discussions, we get kids thinking in new ways about the world that surrounds them, inspiring them to bring the message of environmental stewardship home to their families and friends. In this way, we strive to promote sustainability throughout our many communities, from the youngest members of society up.

Our mission is to bridge the gap between academia and industry through networking events, technical workshops, mentorship, and hands-on learning opportunities. By promoting collaboration, innovation, and ethical practice, we strive to inspire students to advance the built environment and contribute meaningfully to the field of structural engineering.

Strut is committed to exploring, training, and celebrating heels dance while honoring its roots in jazz and embracing its influence within today’s commercial dance industry. By fostering an inclusive and supportive community, Strut equips its members not only to thrive in their craft but also to contribute meaningfully to the cultural landscape of dance at UCI and beyond.

Students For Socialism is the student affiliate of the Party for Socialism and Liberation, a national organization involved in a wide range of struggles, from local battles over affordable housing and racist police brutality, to the fight for a higher minimum wage and union rights, to the global issues of imperialist war and environmental destruction. SFS seeks to merge the struggles of oppressed and exploited people with the fight for socialism. We are united in our belief that capitalism—a system where all wealth and power is held by a small group of billionaires and their state—is the source of the main problems confronting humanity today. It must be replaced by socialism, a system where poor and working people control all the wealth and power of society, using it to plan for and meet the needs of the people and planet.
