Thai Culture Association at UCI comprises of members of various ethnicity with one common goal: to spread the love of Thailand. TCA is dedicated to preserving culture, honoring traditions, giving back to the community, and adhering to all the values from which Thailand's culture was born. Through a constantly active effort to unite people through community service and community participation, people from every ethnicity are welcome to join TCA as they learn to appreciate the many wonders of Thailand.

Our goal is to foster a creative environment for students to learn and teach the art of crochet, knitting, embroidery, and other handcrafts. We hope to donate our group projects to local charities as well as hold workshops to teach various crafts (crochet, knitting, embroidery, and etc).

club_name: The Beautiful Mind Project at UCI
description: The Beautiful Mind Project aims to promote well-rounded and intersectional understandings of mental health in the UC Irvine community, which includes the Muslim community and other student organizations. The Beautiful Mind Project aims to transcend socio-cultural, political, and physical barriers of stigmatization, while also advocating for social justice initiatives that affect these marginalized communities. The Beautiful Mind Project seeks to accomplish this goal by utilizing Islamic principles as a source of and inspiration for mental wellness. By providing diverse, accessible resources, the Beautiful Mind Project advocates for its members a lifestyle that emphasizes the delicate balance between mental, spiritual, and physical health.

A place for people to consume, discuss, discover, learn about, and engage with the horror genre in its many mediums. This includes, but is not limited to films, tv, books, manga, anime, video games, and internet-based mediums. We encourage anyone with any level of 'horror knowledge' or interest in the genre to join us as we dive deep into all things, scary, campy, and weird!

Empowering builders and changemakers to connect, experiment, and launch ventures that make a real difference. The Forge champions authenticity, mutual support, and the kind of progress born from passion rather than posturing. It is the goal of The Forge to connect project-starters and students set on creating something impactful. A community focused on taking the fluff out of business and entrepreneurship organizations to provide a clean space for people that want to support each other. Value will come with effort and time, so The Forge seeks to give back what members put in, creating an organization that is built around those who join.
Working to ensure undergraduate students are able to create innovative and sustainable projects on our campus.

Our mission is to find strength with conversation, community, and, ultimately, patience. We began with the idea of waiting with patients in the hospital waiting room - because no one should have to watch the clock alone. We host speakers and workshops to explore medical narratives, host weekly student-led volunteering at local senior centers, offer pre-health mentorship resources, and also provide other local volunteering opportunities. This is the opportunity to inspire meaningful change through conversational care. See www.patientproject.org for an overview of our core initiatives: conversational care, community journal, and campus collaborations. IG: @patientprojectuciemail: patientproject@uci.eduFB: The Patient Project - UCI

The Philosophy Club is an open and free space for all students interested in Philosophy. We host a wide array of events on several issues pertaining to Philosophy. Our goal is to transcend the boundaries of academic philosophy and open the space for all issues that foster our growth as inquirers. Moreover, we wish to provide a safe, supportive and welcoming environment for all students. We will maintain trust and an ethos of respect for differing viewpoints. Members are expected to be considerate, open-minded and patient when expressing their views and responding to points-of-view with which they disagree. We aim to have a diverse approach to texts and cultivate an inclusive outlook towards philosophical discussion. Events, text-based discussions, movie nights, talks, and membership is open to any and all UCI students. No prerequisite knowledge of Philosophy is necessary. Our discussion and events include introductions to initiate students into the topic. To become official members of the club, please attend the club events and approach the team.For Fall 2024 we will be hosting general meetings at 6pm on Mondays.

club_name: The Shifa Society of Muslim Pre-Health Students
description: The Shifa Society of Muslim Pre-Health Students is a student organization dedicated to the pre-health professional development of members through the abridgment of deen (Islamic religion) with dunya (worldly life) to foster a community of successful health professionals and sustainable Muslims.

club_name: The Student Pharmacist Class Cabinets (Class of 2026)
description: 1. Provide a forum for all students to express their needs and concerns.2. Recognize and address these needs and concerns by acting as mediators between faculty and staff and/or act as a repository of resources for the students.3. Represent all students enrolled at the UCI School of Pharmacy and their interests internally within the UCI community and externally.4. Enrich the academic, professional, and social experiences of all students enrolled at the UCI School of Pharmacy through initiatives, services, and events.

club_name: The Student Pharmacist Class Cabinets (Class of 2027)
description: The Student Pharmacist Class Cabinets (Class of 2027), also known as SPCC2027, aims to serve the students of Doctor of Pharmacy (PharmD) program Class of 2027 as their main student body.

club_name: The Student Pharmacist Class Cabinets (Class of 2028)
description: The purpose of SPCC Class of 2028 shall be to:1. 2. 3. 4. Provide a forum for all students to express their needs and concerns.Recognize and address these needs and concerns by acting as mediators between allstudents, faculty, and staff and/or act as a repository of resources for the students.Represent all students enrolled at UCI and their interests internally within the UCIcommunity and externally.Enrich the academic, professional, and social experiences of all students enrolled at UCIthrough initiatives, services, and events.
We meet regularly to cook and share food with a story. If you're interested in cooking or dining with us, please refer to our website.

club_name: The William F. Buckley Society. Intercollegiate Studies Institute at UCI
description: The William F. Buckley Jr. Society is a community dedicated to the art of debate and the pursuit of truth through Socratic education, critical thinking, and open discourse.

Here at the Women's Network, we are committed to fostering a supportive, non-competitive environment where women uplift one another through intentional communication and meaningful networking. Our mission is to empower women to achieve professional success while cultivating and celebrating their ambition every step of the way.

club_name: The Young Americans for Freedom at UCI
description: The Young Americans for Freedom at UC Irvine stands as a blazing torch of conservative activism, fearlessly defending the sacred right of free speech, upholding the unyielding pillars of individual liberty, free enterprise, traditional values, and a resolute national defense. In a world shadowed by censorship and conformity, we ignite the Anteater spirit with unapologetic courage, rallying students to champion truth through bold engagement, and forge a legacy of freedom that echoes across generations.

club_name: Theme Park Engineering & Design Club at UCI - TPED
description: TPED at UCI aims to bridge the gap between engineering, design, and storytelling by fostering an interdisciplinary community of students at UC Irvine. TPED at UCI encourages creativity and problem-solving through workshops, projects, and competitions and offers professional development opportunities by connecting with industry experts and Imagineering professionals.

The Themed Entertainment Association aims to introduce people to the professional side of the themed entertainment industry and incubate the existing passions and interests of said industry. While the group is professionally driven, it also welcomes fans of themed entertainment. TEA also wishes to connect other individuals with a greater community that shares the common interest of enjoying and wishing to pursue themed entertainment.
Theta Tau is the nation's oldest and largest Fraternity for Engineers. Theta Tau's mission is to develop Engineering Leaders for Service, Professionalism, and Brotherhood.

Tomo No Kai’s expressed purposes are to develop positive social interactions within and outside the club, to promote, continue, and educate ourselves and others of Japanese/Japanese-American culture and issues pertaining thereof, and to render our services to the community.

Our mission statement is to allow underprivileged children from various child care facilities across Southern California receive relief, a medium of expression, and emotional support. We aim to accomplish this goal by providing these children with access to personalized tote bags, essential supplies, and notes of encouragement.

TBS@UCI is an organization dedicated to supporting new and continuing transfer students in the Charlie Dunlop School of Biological Sciences by offering mentorship, community, and opportunities to build up and strengthen themselves, the School, and the UCI community.

The purpose of Triangle shall be to maintain a fraternity of engineers, architects and scientists. It shall carry out its purpose by establishing chapters that develop balanced men who cultivate high moral character, foster lifelong friendships, and live their lives with integrity.

Triathlon Club welcomes student athletes to train and race together. We encourage participation from all levels of athletic ability. We embrace the multisport lifestyle, emphasizing on three main principles: swim, bike, run!

club_name: True Jesus Church Irvine Campus Fellowship (TJCICF)
description: TJC ICF is a small but close-knit Christian campus fellowship centered around weekly Bible studies. We also have different activities and outings throughout the year aimed at edifying one another. The campus fellowship is created by members of True Jesus Church and is directly affiliated with church. Beliefs include Water Baptism, Holy Communion, and Footwashing being directly related to one's salvation; keeping the Sabbath (Saturday) holy under grace; praying earnestly for the Holy Spirit and speaking in tongues.

The purpose of this organization is to promote Turkish language and culture at the University of California, Irvine (UCI), and to unite Turkish speakers, those who identify as Turkish, and all who would like to learn about Turkish language and culture, regardless of their background.
We are a conservative youth- organization committed to identify, educate, train, and organize students to promote principles of freedom, fiscal responsibility, free markets, and limited government.

The U See Eyes pre-optometry club is designed to help prepare students for admission into optometry school and build a network between members. We aim to provide members with the resources and support to become a competitive applicant through volunteering, shadowing and internship opportunities, leadership, and up-to-date information about the field of optometry. U See Eyes also provides the opportunity for members to meet other aspiring students and connect with each other as well as with current optometry professionals.

Uncensored America at UCI is a youth-driven free speech organization dedicated to hosting honest and fun conversations with controversial figures to fight censorship and cancel culture.Our goal is to create a free speech culture to make America free and fun again.

The Undergraduate Business Association (UBA) at UC Irvine is a student-led organization open to all students regardless of major and year. UBA aims to provide students with countless opportunities to explore career interests in business from a variety of industries through our professional events and to foster personal and professional development through our mentorship programs and social events. UBA's executive board reflects a diverse background of individuals who strive to make sure every UBA member has a pleasant and rewarding experience.

The Undergraduate Finance Association strives to assist students in attaining their career goals in the financial field. We are a professional student organization dedicated to providing students with the knowledge, resources, and opportunities that will allow them to excel in the field of finance. Our members hail from a wide range of disciplines, such as Business and Quantitative Economics, Math, and Engineering, as well as Accounting and Management. Our members have the chance to interact with speakers and peers who share a similar passion for finance. UFA provides students with a unique education and networking opportunities, which will dovetail them into successful interviews and work performance at financial firms. Our mission is to provide students with the necessary tools and skills to secure internships and begin their careers in the finance industry. We ensure appropriate guidance for students to reach their specific goals through: Seeking internship opportunities within and outside our corporate network Providing networking and recruitment opportunities with the local insurance, consulting, and investment community, including investment funds, financial advisors, banks, and investment banks Incorporating different levels of involvement ranging from workshops to hands-on student management of an Investment Fund Taking advantage of the knowledge and guidance of Paul Merage faculty MBA student advisors. We work closely with the UCI Career Center, Paul Merage Business School, and the UCI Economics Department to create professional, educational, and networking opportunities for our members.

club_name: Undergraduate Mathematics Committee (formerly Faces in Mathematics)
description: Undergradute Mathematics Committee’s mission is to foster and sustain an inclusive community for all undergraduates interested in pursuing mathematics at University of California, Irvine.

club_name: Undergraduate MD-PhD Society at UC Irvine
description: The Undergraduate MD/PhD Society (UMPS) at UC Irvine is a chapter of a student-led 501(c)(3) nonprofit dedicated to empowering all undergraduate students—especially those who are underserved or underrepresented—to pursue MD/PhD, MD, PhD, and other graduate-level careers in medicine and science. With over 1,200 members across UC San Diego, UCLA, and UC Irvine, UMPS provides clinical training, research preparation, mentorship, and leadership opportunities to help students thrive on their path to advanced study.

club_name: Undergraduate Public Health Association at UCI
description: The purpose of the Public Health Association is to explore and raise awareness of various occupational paths related to the field of public health, and to allow those interested in public health to meet other students with similar class schedules and career interests. Unique volunteer and internship positions are also promoted to members.

Underground AZN Players at UCI is the first student-run AANHPI theatre company spotlighting Asian American, Asian, Native Hawaiian, and Pacific Islander artists in the Anteater community in three ways:1) Producing live theatre performances – including fully staged productions, new play readings, and special workshops showcasing diverse “AZN” voices – for the entire UC Irvine community. 2) Advocating on behalf of students for increased representation of AANHPI artists and narratives in CTSA’s mainstage productions and programming, as the only student-run Asian-American and Asian Affinity Drama Group at UCI Arts.3) Creating events and conversations around socio-political intersections of culture, new performance practices, and authentic storytelling in collaboration with other student groups, faculty initiatives, and professional theatre companies. Through our annual AANHPI Theatre Festival & Open Mic, as well as new play development and fully student-initiated programming, Underground AZN Players continues to celebrate and uplift cross-cultural work across the entire UC Irvine campus, bringing “AZN” student groups and our allies into a safer and stronger community, together.

Our aim is to outreach to and increase retention rates of formerly incarcerated UCI students by connecting them with the resources, and information that may help to increase those students' prospects of success. We strive to provide a space of solidarity, encouragement, wellness, and growth. We only have the insurance provided by the university. We are affiliates of the Underground Scholars Initiative at Cal Berkely, UCLA, and UC Davis.

club_name: Underrepresented Genders in Physics and Astronomy (UNITY) (formerly Women in Physics and Astronomy at UCI)
description: Underrepresented Genders in Physics and Astronomy (UNITY) is a representative body for all folks whose gender identities and/or experiences of gender have been historically marginalized in physics and astronomy at the undergraduate and graduate levels and beyond. Our overarching goal is to create a more diverse community and a supportive environment in physics and astronomy at UCI.

The mission of the Underwater Robotics Project at the University of California, Irvine is to design, build, and operate autonomous underwater robotic systems in the Robosub International Competition while providing students with rigorous, hands-on experience in robotics, autonomy, and engineering systems.The organization aims to advance student education in mechanical, electrical, and software engineering through real-world application, interdisciplinary collaboration. URP @ UCI seeks to foster innovation, technical excellence, teamwork, and professional development while representing UCI in the global robotics community.
We strive to put a dent in Middle Eastern and African poverty by providing humanitarian aid and tools for empowerment.

club_name: UNICEF (United Nations Children's Fund) at UCI
description: UNICEF at UCI is a branch of a larger student-led grassroots movement by the United Nations Children's Fund [UNICEF]. At UNICEF at UCI, there are ample numbers of opportunities to advocate, aid and raise awareness for underserved children and mothers throughout the community and around the world. UNICEF works in more than 190 countries and territories to save and improve children's lives by providing health care and immunizations, clean water and sanitation, nutrition, education, emergency relief and more. UNICEF at UCI upholds these values and goals through community service, fundraising, and awareness on our campus and local community. Together, we are working toward the day when ZERO children die from preventable causes and every child has a safe and healthy childhood without exploitation, discrimination or violence.

At UniConn, our mission is to create meaningful connections that empower students to thrive academically, socially, and personally. We provide a safe and inclusive platform where students can build friendships, find compatible roommates, join communities, and discover opportunities that reflect their identities and interests. By bridging the gaps between people, organizations, and resources, UniConn strengthens campus life and fosters a culture of belonging, collaboration, and growth.

club_name: Unique Representation of Movement (formerly Urban Motus)
description: Unique Representation of Movement (URMO) is a family dedicated to growth and individual expression through movement. Our goal is to uphold the history of dance culture and our team's passion for artistry in an inclusive space to foster the purest representation of ourselves.

Our mission is to gather as many members around us who are Korean or those who are interested in the culture of Korea and help them find people who share the same hobbies or interests and support them with many different events.

club_name: United Nations Association of the United States of America at UCI
description: Our chapter of UNA-USA will be committed to educating ourselves and others on the goals of the United Nations and localizing these goals to our community. Through collaboration and community service, we will spread our knowledge and insight to better support those in need.

club_name: United States Institute for Theatre Technology Student Chapter at UCI
description: The purpose of this organization is to promote technical theatre education through lessons, mentorship, workshops, and hands-on practice. We aim to provide opportunities for professional development, networking, and education. In providing hands-on technical education, we also aim to support the production of student produced shows by providing technical work and support for under supported productions.

Founded in 1994, Uniting Voices has grown from cultural-club choir to the premiere all-gender a cappella group at UCI. Inspired by the power of storytelling and diversity, their talent and hard work have taken them far beyond their humble roots. In just the last few years, the group has been a three-time Best A Cappella Group winner in UCI's annual talent show, Soulstice, a two-time competitor in the Los Angeles A Cappella Festival (LAAF), and the first group to advance to the ICCA Semifinals in UCI Aca-History. In the past years, the group's performances have earned them Best Overall Performance and People's Choice at Soulstice as well as multiple placements in the ICCA Semifinals. As they reach new heights, Uniting Voices continues to captivate audiences with their diverse strengths and shared passion for creating art through a cappella.

club_name: Unmanned Aerial Vehicles at UCI (formerly UAVs at UCI)
description: We are a club dedicated to creating a welcoming community of RC aviation enthusiasts and beginners at the University of California, Irvine.Our aim is to make it easy for students to find a place where they can hang out, connect with fellow enthusiasts, and take to the skies with their UAVs. Whether you're an experienced pilot or new to the hobby.

UPOC seeks to enrich the educational experience for students in the MURP program at UCI by serving as a liaison between student members of color and the professional and academic communities of planning. UPOC's core values are passion, fun, innovation, intellectualism, curiosity, collaboration, and community service.

The purpose of Urban Studies Student Association is to create a support system for UCI undergraduate students who are interested in the field of Urban Studies. USSA strives to provide its members with educational networking opportunities and professional development to enhance their academic experience at UCI.

To educate and empower UCI students by providing practical experience, mentorship, collaboration with industry professionals and networking opportunities in the venture capital field, thereby enhancing their understanding and engagement in the private equity ecosystem.

Established in 2009, Vermillion Vocalists, also known as VEVO, is an all-inclusive a capella group dedicated to creating meaningful musical experiences through vocal performance. Most recognizable in red and black, VEVO is composed of talented individuals who come together not only as performers, but as a close-knit family. As active participants in both UCI's a capella community and in various other communities across college campuses, VEVO embraces togetherness and diversity in every aspect, including the expansive repertoire that ranges from classic hits to today's chart toppers in genres such as pop, hip hop, and R&B.

As a student chapter of The Vertical Flight Society at UCI, we aim to bridge the gap between industry and academia by hosting guest speakers, networking events, company tours, technical workshops, and student competitions. VFS is an international non-profit organization working to advance vertical flight technology. We aim to engage and educate student members in this field, preparing them for careers as professional engineers. We are committed to cultivating leadership skills and encouraging innovation, creativity, and teamwork among our members.

The Video Game Development Club (VGDC) at UC Irvine is devoted to providing community and resources to student game developers. We facilitate opportunities to explore their interests and passions through quarterly student-led game projects, game jams, department workshops, industry speakers, social activities, hardware, and software resources. Whether acting on an interest, or in pursuit of a career, all are welcome, as each and every voice is valuable and contributes to making games what they are.

VSA strives to preserve and promote the Vietnamese culture at UCI through creative and entertaining weekly meetings and by offering a wide range of social and cultural activities geared towards varying member talents and interests.

The mission of Visions for Change is to provide a platform for mentors and mentees to work together in a family-like structure to propose and implement advocacy projects that promote sustainability, student wellness, and positive change for UCI students. Mentors and mentees will have the creative freedom to pitch and develop project ideas to make a change in students' undergraduate experience. Our club prides itself on promoting student wellness and fostering a supportive community where members can develop their interpersonal and professional skills. The skills that mentors and mentees will learn through this program can be applied in all careers, while also giving them the opportunity to contribute to initiatives that they are passionate about. In addition to project development, club members will have the opportunity to participate in professional development workshops, in addition to collaborating and learning from UCI staff and other professionals to gain information regarding ways to enhance the quality of their advocacy projects. Overall, all members of Visions for Change should be working towards addressing short-comings in the UCI undergraduate experience and work towards eliminating these through heart-felt and well-developed community-based projects.

VocaLotus A Cappella is a diverse, coed a cappella group at the University of California, Irvine. Our goal is to grow and perform in a collaborative and uplifting singing environment, while creating a close-knit community.

Through a wide selection of diverse repertoire, Voces aspires to inspire audiences twelve months a year. Our choirs travel throughout the LA area and Orange County area singing in churches, public stages, and high schools, acting as university ambassadors and inspiring through music. During the summer, members have the opportunity to travel internationally and experience musical and cultural immersion, displaying their passion for music and bringing their musical gifts home to the UCI community.

club_name: Volunteer Income Tax Assistance at UCI
description: VITA at UCI offers free income tax return assistance to those in need in the community. We provide assistance to people in need, including low-income people, limited English-speaking people, people with disabilities, and senior people. We serve UCI students, staff, and the nearby communities in need of tax assistance. We help people to correctly file their income tax returns and to understand their tax benefits, which help people to keep their hard-earned money because of our free tax filing service and being able to use every available tax benefit. We also offer UCI students opportunities to contribute to the community and gain hands-on experience.

We (Skin)care at UCI is an organization that is passionate about educating students on the necessity of skincare as a form of self-care. With in-depth research and guidance on the wide range of skincare products offered by many brands, we hope to promote positive changes in students' everyday skincare and self-care behaviors. In order to do this, we will arrange for guest speakers to educate our members, have a strong social media presence to publicly promote our beliefs and skincare tips, and provide members with the opportunity to practice good hygiene and skincare habits.

club_name: Well-being and Nutrition Club at UCI
description: We wanted to create a space where students from all backgrounds could come together and collaborate on recipe sharing, healthy snack making, goal setting, learning about our beautiful bodies, and finding balance among the chaos of student life. Being in University can make it extremely difficult to find a place where we can center ourselves. It can quickly become overwhelming adhering to the demands of school, family, society… you name it. Don’t jeopardize the connection you have with yourself!We encourage you to step back, and explore the principles of nutrition and its relationship to wellbeing. Through us you will enjoy learning about balanced dieting and clean produce, gut health, emotional growth, culture, and self love. We hope to implement some of the science based principles we have been practicing that will promote your definition of happiness and wellbeing.

club_name: West African Dance Group at UCI - WADG
description: The West African Dance Group (WADG) was founded by beautiful, illustrious, and creative African women on the UCI campus in 2008. WADG dancers are a mix of dancers from different African diaspora. We are an organization that embraces our culture and beauty while exuding and promoting confidence through movement. Our take on Afro-Fusion/ Afrobeat dance makes us feel empowered and is our gift to ourselves and others.

club_name: West Coast Credible Messengers at UCI
description: West Coast Credible Messengers at UCI is dedicated to fostering positive change and reducing recidivism by empowering individuals with lived experiences in the criminal legal system to become credible messengers of hope, inspiration, and transformation. Through mentoring, education, and community engagement, we aim to break the cycle of incarceration and support individuals in leading productive and fulfilling lives.

club_name: Women and Youth Supporting Each Other (WYSE)
description: WYSE mentors provide group and one-on-one mentoring by meeting individually with their assigned mentee(s) for a portion of the weekly group session as well as calling their mentee(s) once a week and going on outings. Each weekly session provides education using the WYSE Curriculum which is made up of three units: Self Awareness and Self-Confidence Building, Sexual Health and Decision Making, and Broader Womxn's Issues and Future Options. The WYSE mission is to provide girls with the information, resources, and support necessary to make informed decisions about relationships, sexuality and their futures and to create community change. WYSE mentors at Scholarship Prep in Santa Ana.

club_name: Women in CyberSecurity Student Chapter at UCI - WiCyS
description: The mission of the WiCyS Student Chapter is to build a community within the University of California Irvine (UCI) that promotes women's education, participation, and leadership in the field of cybersecurity. The WiCyS Student Chapter is organized with the following purposes: 1. To decrease the gender disparity in cybersecurity.2. To provide education, mentorship, and networking support to students through the WiCyS community.3. To promote and recruit women in cybersecurity workforce through UCI.

club_name: Women in Information and Computer Sciences
description: Our vision is to encourage women to pursue a college degree and a successful career in the the fields pertaining to Information and Computer Sciences, and to provide them with the support to achieve these goals.

To provide active members with opportunities to learn about women in the legal field, law enforcement, and related fields as well as current issues. To provide an engaging setting for members to meet others with similar interests and/or career goals. And to provide a safe environment for individuals to feel comfortable and supported while learning and participating in all aspects of the organization.

club_name: Women in Leadership at UCI- WIL
description: Women in Leadership is an undergraduate student organization whose purpose is to bring together a community of students at UCI that is interested in the opportunities and potential of women in leadership and business. Open to all majors and backgrounds, our club provides opportunities for our members to connect with successful leaders in our society from a wide variety of fields. Empowering women to believe in themselves and their dreams, our club also promotes leadership opportunities for members to give back to the community.

The mission of this organization is committed to establishing an environment of motivation and mutual support for women pursuing their degree in the sciences, technology, engineering, and mathematics by providing networking, service, camaraderie, and leadership opportunities for our members.

The Women's Basketball Club at UCI is a welcoming space for all UCI students who share a passion for basketball. We are dedicated to fostering an environment where members can learn, improve, and enjoy the game together. We strive for the best in both sports and academics, encouraging members to exceed in both aspects. Through the Women's Basketball Club at UCI, we endeavor to create an environment where growth, passion, and unity flourish. Our commitment to basketball and each other is reflected in our shared journey of self-discovery and athletic achievements.

The Women’s Gaming Club is a community dedicated to supporting female gamers and game developers, encouraging them to share their unique experiences in gaming and their expertise in game development. The club was founded with the mission of challenging stereotypes and biases against women in gaming communities, as well as addressing the underrepresentation of female developers in the gaming industry. We aim to create a welcoming and inclusive environment where women can express themselves freely and contribute to the world of games.Women’s Gaming Club regularly organizes activities like game creation events (e.g., Game Jams), providing opportunities for collaboration and growth. Additionally, we plan to invite accomplished female professionals from renowned gaming companies to UCI for guest lectures, where they can share their insights and career experiences.We warmly welcome individuals of all genders, nationalities, and cultural backgrounds to join us, share their thoughts and ideas about gaming, and contribute to fostering diversity in the gaming industry!

The Women's Lacrosse Club at UCI team is a competitive club sports team governed under the US Lacrosse Women's Collegiate Lacrosse Associates (WCLA) and the Western Women's Lacrosse League (WWLL). The team competes against other universities in California, Nevada, and Arizona and welcomes players of all skill levels, from beginner to advanced. Our mission is to bring women together to share social and athletic experiences while balancing academics as well.

club_name: Women's Law Society at UCI Law School (WLS)
description: The mission of the Women's Law Society (WLS) is two-fold: to promote the academic, personal and professional development of women law students, and to encourage thoughtful discussion of issues related to gender, law and society. WLS furthers these goals by hosting a speaker series; providing mentoring and academic and career development workshops; and connecting students with other organizations in the community focusing on women's issues. WLS is open to all law students.

The Women’s Rowing Club at UCI is a highly competitive program built on teamwork, focus, and determination. Our dedicated and passionate athletes compete against collegiate teams nationwide, while our novice squad welcomes those with no prior rowing experience. Immersed in this ambitious and supportive environment, our student-athletes develop not only as competitors, but as distinguished individuals prepared to excel both on and off the water.

The object and purpose of the Club is to promote knowledge and understanding of the sport of rugby within the UC Irvine community and to create a fair and safe playing environment within the rules and regulations of the game.

Women's Soccer Club is an intercollegiate team in a competitive league (USCCS & NIRSA soccer) that plays against teams all across California, Arizona and Oregon. This club allows girls who have an interest in soccer to compete in a challenging environment, while making strong bonds with teammates.

club_name: Women's Ultimate Club (formerly Women's Ultimate Frisbee Club at UCI)
description: Women's Ultimate is a competitive frisbee team that travels to different colleges to compete in tournaments. We welcome players of all levels who are interested in learning the sport, even if throwing a disc is unnatural for you! Our club is about the love of the game and having fun! Expect a great outdoor workout while meeting new people and learning a new sport.

We provide a competitive environment for women who wish to play volleyball in college without the time demands of a collegiate varsity (NCAA) team. We encourage the improvement of every player while providing a positive experience for coaches and players to push each other and have fun.

club_name: Women's Water Polo Club at UCI
description: What: A competitive women's water polo club working to enhance the experience of its members in a team directed environment. For: Girls with or without previous experience in the sport of water polo and wish to enhance and continue their experience in a fun and competitive atmosphere.

At UCI, the Wushu club aims to foster a competitive, yet inviting environment for Wushu athletes of all skill levels. Wushu, as practiced at UCI, is a non-contact Chinese martial art, emphasizing on coordination and performance. Wushu represents a collection of all Chinese martial arts, but often, the term is used to refer to the more-modern styles of its traditional counterpart, Kung Fu. For more information stop by to try out the sport first hand (no club fees for the first practice!).

club_name: XI ISLE Chinese Drama Club at UCI
description: To create a space for Chinese-language performance, cross-cultural storytelling, and collaborative theatrical production. We hope to stage original or adapted works, organize workshops, and build a community for students interested in exploring identity and culture through performance. And we have completed a comedy production on a stage at UCI that drew an audience of over a thousand people.
To make Shakespeare and classical theatre accessible, understandable, and enjoyable to everyone.

We are an organization that allows for people to meet, play, and discuss the Yugioh trading card game. We are open to all players, from casual to competitive, and aim to foster a welcoming environment where we can have fun and enjoy the game as a community.

Zamana at UCI is an award-winning Bollywood Fusion dance team that participates in circuit competitions across the nation. Along with a foundation in Bollywood, the team incorporates a variety of different styles, including hip hop, bhangra, jazz, kuthu, contemporary, and classical. Founded in 2009, Zamana has performed at prestigious events across the country, and has been invited to audition for America's Got Talent. Check us out on Instagram, TikTok, Facebook, or YouTube for more information!

ZotBins is an innovative smart waste bin system designed to optimize waste management efficiency and promote sustainable practices. By collecting and analyzing data on waste diversion rates—specifically, the proportion of incorrectly placed trash items relative to the total waste volume (e.g. glass bottle in the trash bin instead of recycle bin)—we aim to enhance campus-wide waste management practices.

description: The purpose of Zotbotics is to provide a community where students interested in the field of robotics can work on fully functional robots and apply their skills in mechanical engineering, electronics, and computer science.

Zotckets is a student-led organization dedicated to encouraging students to explore engineering through hands-on experience in rocketry. Our goal is to help students design, manufacture, and launch their own L1 rockets, enabling them to receive certification. Through club-facilitated workshops and events, we aim to create a community where students can engage in a meaningful project alongside their peers, enhance their resumes, and pursue their professional or personal goals. Anyone is welcome to join the club, regardless of experience or major, as we aim to create a community that caters to students from diverse backgrounds. In the long term, we plan to expand our organization into an interdisciplinary club that fosters innovation in rocketry across various STEM fields.

ZotCon's top priority is to create a safe space for anyone who enjoys Japanese mainstream culture. Our mission is to let anyone and everyone who are interested, ranging from students just dipping their toes into Japanese culture to those who have dedicated their lives researching and experiencing it, come together and express themselves and their love for the culture in any way or form.
